commits.pr_title: [RL] Declare weight ownership and layout on ParamMeta
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Implements steps 1–3 of RFC #63215: a `WeightSource` now declares which trainer ranks own each parameter, and how it is laid out across them, on `ParamMeta`. Every engine plans from that declaration instead of a runtime exchange, and a source exposes `iter_full()` and/or `iter_local()` instead of one iterator plus per-backend hooks (`held_names`, `groups`, `M2NWeightSource`).

Step 4 (NCCL broadcast from more than one sender, i.e. pipeline-parallel trainers on NCCL) is left to #62557, which this makes simpler: the per-sender plan can be read straight off `ParamMeta.owners`.

## Claims

- **One ownership declaration for every backend.** `ParamMeta` gains `owners` (global trainer ranks), `mesh_shape` and `placements` (`Replicate` / `Shard`, `torch.chunk` semantics). Metadata is identical on every rank, so engines plan without exchanging it.
- **Two explicit iteration modes.** `iter_full()` yields `(name, full tensor)` and `iter_local()` yields `(name, this rank's piece)`, each only for the names the rank owns, in metadata order. NCCL broadcast, IPC and sharded RDT use `iter_full()`; NCCL M2N uses `iter_local()`. Each engine checks the mode it needs at `trainer_init` (`source.implements_iter_full()` / `implements_iter_local()`).
- **`ModuleSource` covers plain, FSDP2 and DTensor modules for every backend.** It reads owners and placements from each DTensor's mesh, which replaces the M2N-specific `DTensorModuleSource`.
- **Sharded RDT keeps partial ownership** (pipeline stages, expert parallelism, or both), now from `owners` instead of `held_names()`. A rank still gathers and serves only the experts it holds.
- **Engines reject layouts they cannot send at `trainer_init`:**
  - NCCL: every parameter's first owner must be rank 0, its single sender.
  - IPC: every rank must own every parameter.
  - M2N: owners must be all trainer ranks, with at most a 2-D mesh.
  - RDT: owner ranks must exist, and metadata must agree across ranks (digest).
- **`WeightSource.metadata` is a `functools.cached_property`, enforced when the subclass is defined.** Engines read it repeatedly and it must not change.
- **Docs:** `base.md` rewrites the `WeightSource` section, and every engine page gains a Limitations section stating which trainer layouts it accepts. Only sharded RDT takes pipeline-parallel trainers today.

## Validation

**End-to-end, bit-exact.** Each run syncs two updated checkpoints, then compares a byte digest of every device tensor against a fresh server loaded from the final checkpoint. The bench is the [weight-update bench](https://github.com/hao-aaron/vllm-state-transition-verifier/tree/sharded-trainer-bench-declared/scripts/vllm_weight_update_client/bench), run on 4×GB200 with a TP=2 server on 2 GPUs and the trainer on the other 2 (IPC shares GPUs 0–1).

| Backend | Trainer layout | Model | Tensors compared / exercised | Mismatches | Median sync |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| sharded RDT | FSDP=2 | Qwen3-0.6B | 678 / 452 | 0 | 0.142 s |
| sharded RDT | PP=2 | Qwen3-0.6B | 678 / 452 | 0 | 0.175 s |
| sharded RDT | FSDP=2, EP=2 | small DeepSeek-V2 MoE | 146 / 112 | 0 | 0.050 s |
| NCCL M2N | FSDP=2 | Qwen3-0.6B | 678 / 452 | 0 | 0.144 s |
| NCCL M2N | TP=2 | Qwen3-0.6B | 678 / 452 | 0 | 0.134 s |
| NCCL | FSDP=2 | Qwen3-0.6B | 678 / 452 | 0 | 0.083–0.088 s (main: 0.082–0.088 s) |
| IPC | FSDP=2 | Qwen3-0.6B | 678 / 452 | 0 | 0.145 s |

- NCCL was run as 4 interleaved pairs against upstream main, since it is the backend whose send path is shared with existing users; the other rows are single runs.
- "Exercised" tensors differ between the starting weights and the final checkpoint, so they only match if the sync wrote them.
- In the EP=2 run each expert is owned by a single rank (36 experts per rank), so no expert is gathered across EP ranks.
- `examples/rl/rlhf_sharded_rdt_small_ep.py` (Qwen1.5-MoE, 2 FSDP trainer ranks → 2 DP/EP vLLM ranks) passes: `[ok] weights moved on sync 0 and replay was stable on sync 1`.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
# one configuration; see the bench README for the rest
python scripts/vllm_weight_update_client/bench/run_bench.py \
  --model-a $CKPT/A --update $CKPT/v1 --update $CKPT/v2 \
  --backend sharded_rdt --layout pp=2 --launcher ray --source-api declared \
  --server-gpus 0,1 --trainer-gpus 2,3 --warmup 1 --iters 3 --audit \
  -- --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 2048 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5
```

</details>

**Unit tests:**

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py \
  tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer_m2n.py \
  tests/distributed/test_sharded_rdt_trainer.py \
  tests/distributed/test_sharded_rdt_producer.py
```

| File | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `test_weight_transfer.py` | 113 passed, 23 skipped |
| `test_weight_transfer_m2n.py` | 82 passed |
| `test_sharded_rdt_trainer.py` | 22 passed |
| `test_sharded_rdt_producer.py` | 66 passed |

`test_weight_transfer.py` was rerun after merging main (737b5a52bc), which adds the NCCL rendezvous tests from #63460; the other three rows are from the pre-merge head (404b4ffba8).

No model evaluation: the change moves the same bytes, which the bit-exact audit checks directly.

## Details

**Why declare ownership.** Each backend had grown its own way to say which rank holds what: `held_names()` plus an all-gather for sharded RDT, `M2NWeightSource` with per-parameter layouts for M2N, and nothing for NCCL and IPC. Declaring it once on `ParamMeta`, identically on every rank:

- gives every engine the same plan without a runtime exchange;
- lets a backend reject a layout it cannot send up front;
- is what multi-sender NCCL (#62557) and partitioned M2N (#62853) need as input.

**Owned-only iteration.** A rank iterates only what it owns. For Megatron PP=2, that is exactly what each stage can produce without communicating. A framework that broadcasts every weight to every stage can declare `owners=None` and do that broadcast inside `iter_full()`, which keeps NCCL working today. Either mode may run collectives among a parameter's owners, such as an FSDP all-gather per tensor or per layer.

**Per-tensor yields cost nothing when the source gathers in batches.** On main, `iter_groups()` existed because one collective per tensor is slow on a per-expert MoE (~37k tensors). The saving comes from batching the gather, not from yielding a group per generator resume. A source can still gather a layer at a time and yield its tensors one by one (the bench's `DeclaredGatherSource` does). Microbenchmark, 2×GB200, 37,050 tensors in 95 groups, each sharded across 2 ranks and all-gathered, median of 3 after warmup:

| Source | Time per sync |
| --- | --- |
| one all-gather per tensor | 4514 ms |
| one all-gather per group, yielded per tensor and regrouped as `_iter_owned_groups` does (this PR) | 577 ms |
| one all-gather per group, yielded per group (main's `iter_groups` override) | 591 ms |

**Breaking changes to the trainer-side API**, which shipped in recent releases:

- `WeightSource.__iter__`, `held_names()`, `groups()` and `iter_groups()` are removed; implement `iter_full()` and declare `owners`.
- `vllm/distributed/weight_transfer/m2n_source.py` (`M2NWeightSource`, `ManifestM2NWeightSource`, `DTensorModuleSource`) is removed; use `ModuleSource`, or a `WeightSource` with `iter_local()` and declared placements. M2N sources now yield torch tensors only; the raw-pointer / CUDA array interface buffers from #60934 are dropped.
- `metadata` changes from a method to a `cached_property` (`source.metadata`, not `source.metadata()`).
- Sharded RDT now requires `TrainerInitInfo.rank` to equal the default process group rank, and raises at `trainer_init` if it does not. It used to take the rank from `torch.distributed` and ignore `TrainerInitInfo.rank`. Owners are declared in `TrainerInitInfo.rank` numbering, and the producer servers are gathered over the default group, so the two must agree.

**Limitations:**

- NCCL and IPC still reject pipeline-parallel trainers (documented as in progress).
- M2N accepts only sources owned by all trainer ranks (#62853 is the follow-up).
- `ModuleSource` declares DTensors with `Partial` or strided (FSDP+TP) placements as replicated, and gathers them in `iter_local()`.

**Not duplicating existing work.** This implements RFC #63215; no other open PR does. #62557 (NCCL per-update source ranks) and #62853 (partitioned M2N source groups) are follow-ups that would build on `ParamMeta.owners` rather than their own ownership plumbing.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][MoE] Add H200 FP8 fused MoE config for Beam-1.0 TP8
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Reflection Beam-1.0 FP8 on H200 runs TP8 with `--moe-backend triton`, as in its recipe. There is no tuned config for its fused MoE shape (`E=256, N=320`, fp8_w8a8), so every layer uses the default config. This PR adds a tuned H200 config for that shape. It also lets `benchmark_moe.py` time the per-token activation / per-channel weight FP8 path that Beam's compressed-tensors checkpoint runs, and parse `BeamForCausalLM`. Follow-up to #62074.

## Claims

- Fused MoE on 1xH200, Beam-1.0 TP8 shape, per-token FP8 path: 3-19% faster at 96-512 tokens when replaying top-k ids recorded from Beam's real weights, and 9-45% faster at 96-1536 tokens with uniform random routing. At 1024 tokens the kernel goes from 31% to 57% of the HBM bound.
- One TP8 rank of Beam-1.0 FP8 on 1xH200 (all 52 layers, dummy weights, uniform simulated routing): a decode step at 128 and 256 requests takes 9.4% and 16.7% less time.
- Up to 64 tokens and from 2048 tokens the file holds the default config, so small-batch decode and prefill do not change. With DFlash2 (recipe: 7 draft tokens), a verify step has 8 rows per request, so 12-192 requests land in the range that gets faster.
- `benchmark_moe.py` now times the kernel variant the model runs: for compressed-tensors checkpoints with `strategy: token` input activations it uses per-token activation and per-channel weight scales. Before, it always timed per-tensor FP8.

## Validation

### Kernel with recorded routing (1xH200)

Top-k ids recorded from Beam-1.0 FP8 with real weights (first 6 layers, so MoE layers 3-5, TP1), decode batches of M requests over two corpora: Python and Markdown files from site-packages, and wikitext-103. They are replayed on the TP8 shape (`E=256, N=320, K=5120`, top-8, per-token FP8) with this file and with the default config. 24 recorded steps per M in one CUDA graph, median of 7 replays, µs per step.

| M | code corpus: default → this PR | wikitext: default → this PR | uniform random: default → this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 213.9 → 214.0 (+0.0%) | 180.4 → 180.0 (-0.2%) | 313.5 → 313.7 (+0.1%) |
| 96 | 244.5 → 229.8 (-6.0%) | 211.2 → 204.7 (-3.1%) | 357.9 → 326.1 (-8.9%) |
| 128 | 280.5 → 253.2 (-9.7%) | 239.1 → 223.3 (-6.6%) | 387.7 → 337.9 (-12.8%) |
| 256 | 384.7 → 311.4 (-19.1%) | 339.2 → 277.4 (-18.2%) | 468.4 → 357.8 (-23.6%) |
| 512 | 445.4 → 390.2 (-12.4%) | 414.0 → 357.3 (-13.7%) | 488.3 → 397.3 (-18.6%) |

Real routing is not uniform: a decode batch of 128 touches 156 (code) or 133 (wikitext) of 256 experts per layer, against 252 for uniform routing, and the busiest expert gets 76-85 rows. So these steps load fewer experts and are shorter than the uniform ones.

### Kernel with uniform routing (1xH200)

`benchmark_moe.benchmark_config` on the per-token path (`per_act_token_quant=True`), random gating, CUDA graph of 10 calls, 100 iterations, median of 3 runs. "Bound" is the expert weights that uniform routing touches, `256 * (1 - (1 - 8/256)^M) * 4.92 MB`, over 4.8 TB/s; FP8 compute is below that at every M here.

| M | bound µs | default µs (of bound) | this PR µs (of bound) | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 96 | 250.1 | 366.2 (68%) | 334.4 (75%) | -8.7% |
| 128 | 258.2 | 398.5 (65%) | 346.6 (74%) | -13.0% |
| 256 | 263.2 | 475.2 (55%) | 365.1 (72%) | -23.2% |
| 512 | 264.3 | 497.8 (53%) | 407.0 (65%) | -18.2% |
| 1024 | 266.5 | 856.7 (31%) | 470.1 (57%) | -45.1% |
| 1536 | 268.7 | 902.0 (30%) | 519.7 (52%) | -42.4% |

At 1-64 tokens the tuned configs were within -4% to +0.3% of the default here, and +1.9% at 64 on the recorded code corpus, so the file keeps the default config there.

### One TP8 rank of Beam-1.0 FP8 (1xH200)

All 52 layers and 256 experts; attention heads and widths are one TP8 rank's share (6 Q heads, 1 KV head, expert width 320). Dummy weights with `VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY=uniform_random`, `--moe-backend triton`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`. Arms ran in one container in the order default, tuned, tuned, default. ms per decode step, median of 4 runs; spread within an arm is under 0.3%.

| | default | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| decode, 16 requests | 12.13 | 12.12 | -0.1% |
| decode, 128 requests | 25.95 | 23.51 | -9.4% |
| decode, 256 requests | 31.67 | 26.38 | -16.7% |
| 8K prefill chunk | 180.6 | 180.6 | 0.0% |

This run used the tuned configs at 1-64 tokens as well; the file now holds the default there, which only matters for the 16-request row.

### Correctness

Only Triton tile parameters change. At the Beam shape and M = 96, 128, 256, 1024 and 1536, the output with this file and with the default config both have a mean relative error of 1.41-1.44% against the per-column reference in `tests/kernels/moe/test_triton_moe_ptpc_fp8.py` (its threshold is 5%). Both configs use `BLOCK_SIZE_K=128`, and the outputs were the same.

`benchmark_moe.py --model reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-FP8 --tp-size 8 --dtype fp8_w8a8 --batch-size 1 128 1024` runs on this branch and prints `Benchmarking per-token activation and per-channel weight FP8.` before the timings (checked on an L4, which has no config file and uses the default config). The tuning run above used the same `benchmark_config` path.

## Details

- Dummy weights route almost every token of a step to the same 8 experts, so each expert sees many rows and larger M tiles win. Without uniform simulated routing, the proxy above shows this file 9.8% and 13.0% slower at 128 and 256 requests. The recorded real routing sits much closer to uniform than to that.
- Per-tensor and per-token FP8 read the same config file name. For this shape, configs tuned on the per-tensor path time within 1% of these on the per-token path.
- The search space was pruned to keep tuning near half an hour: `BLOCK_SIZE_M` 16 up to 128 tokens, 16-32 up to 512, 16-64 above; `GROUP_SIZE_M` in {1, 16, 64}. The pruning was in my tuning script, not in `benchmark_moe.py`.
- Not covered: H100, TP4 (`N=640`), DFlash2 verify, and the full model. 503 GB FP8 needs 8xH200, which I did not run. The recorded routing comes from 3 early MoE layers; later layers may route differently.

Not a duplicate: no open PR adds a fused MoE config for `E=256,N=320`, and none adds per-token FP8 to `benchmark_moe.py`. The open `benchmark_moe.py` PRs change model parsing or error handling (#62526, #49088, #50711, #51353), or add zipf-skewed expert loads (#57100), which is a separate axis from the quantization path here. #61688 (runtime Triton autotune, draft) would make static configs less important if it lands.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Preserve running request prefixes across LRU store batches
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Preserve the reusable head of CPU-offloaded prefixes while their requests are still running, across store batches and KV groups. Related to [the unfinished-request observation in #58804](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58804#issuecomment-6098736505); this addresses that eviction pattern rather than the issue's entire throughput regression.

## Claims

- Positioned keys share a provisional request rank, with later token positions evicted first across batches.
- `insert(key, chunk, req_context)` assigns new chunks their final provisional rank directly. First observations still handle resident prefixes reused by load/store and anchor requests before allocation retries.
- Finalization commits recency and ARC frequency accounting; transfer pinning, newer shared accesses, reset and keys without positions retain their behavior.

## Validation

Latest review revision: Linux x86_64, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu, based on the bot-merged head `b27bfdfde95e835043749b82bc3d4e2c558eace0`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/test_factory.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/base.py vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/lru.py vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/arc.py vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/manager.py tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/test_factory.py docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md
```

76 manager/policy tests and 500 tiering/scheduler tests passed. All applicable hooks passed. The two new insertion-contract cases fail on the merged head because `insert` lacks `req_context`; with the revision, ready and pending chunks both evict tail before head without a follow-up access call. The original running-prefix regression tests previously gave 11 failed/2 passed against the unmodified base.

A native CPU replay through `LLM` used a two-layer tiny Llama, dummy weights, float32, greedy decoding, two 192-token prompts, block size 32 and eight offload slots. A remains unfinished while B adds pressure. Aborting A, clearing only model-side prefix caching and replaying A gives the same result before and after this interface revision: 64 cached tokens, 2 actual CPU KV blocks loaded and output token IDs `[11, 11, 11, 11]`. A test-only worker synchronously copies real CPU KV pages; the installed native extensions are shared by both runs. This validates usable KV reuse and observed output, not model quality or CUDA transfer behavior.

Manager-only timings, five runs per row, nine groups and batches of eight; median [min,max] milliseconds:

| Chunks/group | Merged PR head | Insertion revision |
|---|---:|---:|
| 64 | 1.980 [1.805,3.454] | 1.807 [1.732,2.703] |
| 256 | 8.911 [7.935,13.120] | 7.887 [7.435,12.620] |
| 1024 | 39.069 [37.165,362.716] | 34.581 [33.813,321.299] |

These are bookkeeping measurements; GPU TTFT and serving throughput were not measured in this review revision.

## Details

Insertion previously made an unfinished request's head older than its tail until finalization. Evicting the head makes every remaining suffix unreachable by contiguous-prefix lookup.

LRU uses `(request_rank, -token_position)` and the existing lazy heap update/compaction paths. The request rank is anchored at first observation; new chunks receive it inside `insert`, while existing resident accesses preserve any newer shared recency. This avoids revisiting the full prefix after every store batch. Cache reset invalidates provisional state. Chunks remain evictable and finalization still commits recency.

Custom `CachePolicy` implementations must accept the additional `req_context` insertion argument; policies that do not use it can ignore it. The custom-policy guide and ARC implementation reflect that interface. ARC frequency promotion remains at finalization.

The fix is distinct from optional in-flight pin protection (#57813), session-aware policies (#50422), GPU-local reuse recording (#57746) and KVCR recency changes (#60469); those target different policies or access sources. This revision addresses the existing review request on #61050.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Fix double pinning of 3D MoE LoRA and EP dummy LoRA sizing
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #61635.

Two small fixes in `LoRAModelManager` for 3D MoE LoRA:

- After stacking, the `experts.base_layer` entry shares its gate_up tensors with the `experts` entry, so the pin loop pinned them twice. Pop the `base_layer` entry at the end of the 3D branch, same as `_convert_3d_to_2d_moe_lora` already does.
- `create_dummy_lora` sized the 3D MoE warmup dummy by local experts, but `_stack_moe_lora_weights` reshapes by `global_num_experts`. Size the dummy by `global_num_experts` so it works when `ep_size` does not divide the warmup rank.

The first fix needs a third change to be safe: `lora_device = next(iter(first_lora.lora_a))` returned a tensor, not a device, so a packed first entry made `str(lora_device) == "cpu"` False and skipped pinning entirely. Once `base_layer` is gone the first entry is the packed `experts` one, so pinning would silently turn off. Read `.device` from the first non-None tensor instead. This also makes packed LoRAs (e.g. a q/v-only adapter on `qkv_proj`) get pinned, which was previously skipped.

Note this device check was also proposed in #44149 (closed as stale).

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py tests/lora/test_lora_weights.py
```

New CPU tests (`pin_memory` is wrapped to count calls, so no CUDA needed):
- `test_pin_memory_for_packed_lora`: packed LoRA is pinned, including when the first sub-LoRA is None.
- `test_3d_moe_lora_pinned_once`: only the `experts` entry is left and each tensor is pinned once.
- `test_dummy_3d_moe_lora_is_sized_by_global_experts`: dummy rank dimension is `rank * global_num_experts` for ep_size 1, 2, 3.

## Test Result

On current main the new tests fail (6 of 7 cases; the ep_size=1 case passes either way) and pass with the change. The existing LoRA unit tests pass (42 passed). `ruff check` and `ruff format` are clean.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Never block in ZmqConnection.send()
commits.pr_body: ## Purpose Part of #63602 (gap 1). `ControlConnection.send()` is documented as non-blocking (`control/base.py`: "ControlConnection.send() must not block"), but `ZmqConnection.send()` called `dealer.send(data)` without `NOBLOCK`, at libzmq's default `SNDHWM` and with no `SNDTIMEO`. Once the queue toward a peer that stops reading fills, the send blocks. Every caller holds the tiering manager lock: the tier-poll thread holds it for a whole round, and `OffloadingConnectorScheduler._acquire_step()` waits on it with no timeout. A blocked send therefore stalls healthy-peer servicing and the engine's next scheduler step. This PR: - Sends with `zmq.NOBLOCK` at an explicit `SNDHWM` (1000, unchanged from the libzmq default but no longer implicit) and raises `ConnectionError` when the queue is full. `P2PSession._do_send` already marks the connection dead on any send error, so a stalled peer is reaped and its pending work fails over to local prefill. #63664 routes the ConnectAck send through the same path. - Bounds DEALER `LINGER` to 500 ms. While writing the test I found that, with the default (-1), closing a DEALER that still has messages queued for an unreachable peer makes `Context.destroy(linger=0)` hang forever. The context-level linger only applies to sockets that are still open. Before this change that path was rare, since a full queue blocked the sender first; now that queued-then-dead is the normal failure path, it has to be bounded. - Leaves `ZMQ_IMMEDIATE` at its default of 0. With `IMMEDIATE=1`, a `NOBLOCK` send fails before the TCP connect completes, which would break the `ConnectMsg` sent right after `connect()`. On the issue's policy question (fail now vs. retry on later polls): this fails now. Control messages are small, so a full queue means the peer went 1000 messages without reading while its TCP connection stayed up. That isn't short-lived backpressure, and a retry outbox would need its own bound plus ordering against the pre-ack queue. Not a duplicate: the only open PRs referencing #63602 are #63628 (gap 4) and #63664 (gap 5). #63207 changes the DEALER monitor teardown, not `send()`. ## Test plan New `TestZmqTransportConnectivity::test_send_raises_instead_of_blocking_when_queue_full`: a real DEALER connects to a port with no listener, with `_SNDHWM` patched to 2. `send()` must raise `ConnectionError` within 1 s, and `transport.close()` must return. ``` venv/bin/pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_zmq_transport.py::TestZmqTransportConnectivity::test_send_raises_instead_of_blocking_when_queue_full venv/bin/pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/control/zmq.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_zmq_transport.py ``` ## Test results - New test with the old blocking `send()`: hangs in `zmq/sugar/socket.py:send`, called from `ZmqConnection.send` (faulthandler dump at 20 s). - New test with this change, but without the linger bound: `send()` raises, then the test hangs in `ZmqTransport.close()` → `Context.destroy()`. - With this change: passes. - Full P2P suite (`tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p`): 312 passed, CPU-only (pyzmq 27.1.0, libzmq 4.3.5). - pre-commit: passed. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Hold promotions after a cache reset until jobs report
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`reset_cache()` in the `OffloadingConnector` scheduler releases the CPU-tier chunks of in-flight transfer jobs at once, but the workers may still write those chunks until they report the jobs. With secondary tiers, a lookup in that window can promote a secondary-tier hit into one of the released chunks, and the late worker write then overwrites it, so a later load hands the GPU wrong KV. This PR adds an `OffloadingManager.on_reset_flushed()` hook, called once the workers have reported every job flushed by the reset, and `TieringOffloadingManager` holds promotions from `reset_cache()` until then.

It is a standalone bugfix on `main` and also applies to a single node.

## Claims

- With `TieringOffloadingSpec` and at least one secondary tier, no promotion into the CPU tier starts after a cache reset until the workers have reported every job the reset flushed. This covers lookups from the scheduler and from tiers that serve peers through their `ParentManager` (`p2p`, `kvcr`). A late DMA of a flushed store, or any other worker write still pending, can no longer land on a chunk a promotion has just filled.
- Lookups keep running in that window: CPU-tier hits are served as before, and a chunk found only in a secondary tier is a miss, so the request recomputes it (or the peer is told it is absent).
- Without secondary tiers (`CPUOffloadingSpec`, or `TieringOffloadingSpec` without tiers), nothing is held (see Details for why it is not needed there). The scheduler still waits for the flushed jobs' reports before calling the hook, so after a reset with jobs in flight the engine keeps stepping until they arrive, normally on the next step.
- While the scheduler waits, the engine keeps stepping even with no request left (`has_pending_push_work()`), so the flush reaches the workers and their reports come back on an idle engine too.
- The scheduler logs when it starts and stops waiting for the reports, and warns once if that lasts more than 60 s; the check runs on every step, including the empty steps of an idle engine.

## Validation

**Regression through `LLM`** (GPU): `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py::test_tiering_cache_reset_resumes_promotions_on_idle_engine`. `facebook/opt-125m`, `TieringOffloadingSpec` with an `fs` tier, `async_scheduling=False`. The engine core and its worker run in the test process (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`). A prefix is stored down to the `fs` tier; then the worker's job reports are withheld behind a `threading.Event` while another prompt's stores are issued, so `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)` always finds them in flight (the test asserts that the hold started). The gate is opened, the idle engine is stepped until the hold is released, and the prefix must be promoted back from the `fs` tier (`num_cached_tokens == len(prefix)`). No retries and no log parsing.

On a DGX Spark (GB10), with `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-00b6c4c565` and this branch's changed Python files on top, this test and `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_worker.py` pass (18 passed). An earlier revision without the `has_pending_push_work()` change failed with `TimeoutError: timed out after 30 s waiting for promotions to resume`.

**Scheduler-level tests** (CPU), in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py`, on a real `Scheduler` whose `OffloadingConnector` runs the real `TieringOffloadingSpec` manager with an `example` secondary tier. A finished request leaves real store jobs in flight, the reset goes through `Scheduler.reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)`, `schedule()` delivers `jobs_to_flush`, and the worker reports come back through `update_from_output()`. Only the workers are played, since the CPU job has no GPU transfers.

- `test_cache_reset_holds_promotions_until_flushed_jobs_report[True|False]`: `Scheduler.has_requests()` stays true until the flushed jobs report, the next step flushes exactly the in-flight jobs, and a secondary-tier-only key is a miss until their reports arrive and promotes after; without secondary tiers nothing is held. Without the `has_pending_push_work()` change it fails on `assert scheduler.has_requests()`.
- `test_cache_reset_fence_ignores_reports_of_other_jobs`: a late report of a job completed before the reset does not count as a flushed job's report.
- `test_cache_reset_without_in_flight_jobs_holds_nothing`: a reset with nothing in flight calls `on_reset_flushed()` at once and holds nothing.
- `test_cache_reset_fence_held_too_long_warns_on_idle_steps`: with a monkeypatched `time.monotonic` in the scheduler module, the 60 s warning fires on an empty step with no request left. It fails if the check runs only on lookups, as it did before.

- `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py::test_held_promotions_answer_peer_lookups_with_miss`: a real `P2PSecondaryTierManager` serves a peer under a real `TieringOffloadingManager`, next to an `example` tier that holds the key; a second P2P manager is the peer, and only the control and NIXL transports are faked (the existing loopback fakes). The peer's `LookupMsg` goes through the real `serve_external_requests()` path: after `reset_cache()` it is answered MISS and nothing is submitted to the `example` tier; after `on_reset_flushed()`, the same lookup starts the promotion. It fails if the hold is ignored. (`p2p` is the lightest in-tree serving tier; `kvcr` needs the external `kvcr` package.)
- `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py::test_held_promotions_keep_primary_hits`: while held, a CPU-tier chunk is still a hit; `test_reset_holds_promotions_until_flushed`: `reset_cache()` holds promotions and `on_reset_flushed()` releases them.

**Suites** (CPU-only container):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_file_mapper.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector
# 1289 passed, 1 failed (on 71294c2e9a)
```

The one failure, `test_worker.py::test_register_packed_kv_caches_skips_scratch_group`, needs a GPU and fails the same way on `main`. The new `LLM` test runs in the "V1 KV Connectors" GPU step (`pytest -m 'not cpu_test' v1/kv_connector/unit`).

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the changed files, and mypy reports no new errors in them.

There is still no reproducer of the data race itself: it needs a late worker DMA to land after a promotion's copy into the same chunk, which a test cannot force on real hardware.

## Details

**Root cause.** `reset_cache()`, reached through `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)` (`POST /reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true`, or `pause_generation(clear_cache=True)`), adds every in-flight job to `jobs_to_flush`, resets the manager, which frees their CPU-tier chunks, and drops later worker reports of those jobs through `_stale_job_threshold`. The workers submit and wait for the flushed jobs in `handle_preemptions()` of the next step they run. The scheduler builds that same step first, and its lookups run before any worker has seen the flush. On a secondary-tier hit, `TieringOffloadingManager.lookup()` reserves a free CPU-tier chunk (`_initiate_promotion()` → `primary_tier.prepare_write()`), which may be one the reset has just released, and the tier copies into it from the engine core after `on_schedule_end()`. Nothing orders that copy against the worker's DMA into the same chunk. If the DMA lands last, the chunk holds stale KV (or KV from blocks the GPU already reused) under the promoted key, and the next load hands it to the GPU. `TieringOffloadingManager.reset_cache()` already drains the secondary tiers' own transfers for exactly this reason ("preferable to silent corruption from reusing primary slots while a transfer is mid-copy"); the workers' transfers were not covered.

The scheduler is not the only caller of `lookup()`. Tiers that serve external requests (`p2p`, `kvcr`) call it through their `ParentManager` from `serve_external_requests()`, in `on_schedule_end()` and on the tier-poll thread, and such a lookup promotes from any other secondary tier the same way.

**Why only promotions.** A promotion is the only write to a CPU-tier chunk that does not come from a worker. A worker submits the flushed stores and waits for them before it submits any job of a later step, and a load, or a secondary tier's read for a cascade or a peer, only uses a chunk whose post-reset store has completed. So a late worker write either finishes before anything that depends on the chunk or is overwritten by it. That is why lookups keep serving CPU-tier hits during the hold, and why engines without secondary tiers hold nothing.

**Fix.**

- `OffloadingManager.on_reset_flushed()` is new, a no-op by default: it is called once the workers have reported every job in flight at the last `reset_cache()`, so blocks that reset freed are no longer written by them.
- `TieringOffloadingManager.reset_cache()` holds promotions when it has secondary tiers, and `on_reset_flushed()` releases them. While held, its `lookup()` returns `MISS` for a chunk that is not in the CPU tier, without querying the secondary tiers, whoever calls it. `MISS` rather than `RETRY`: `RETRY` would stall the request (and keep a peer's lookup pending) until the hold is released, while the chunk can simply be recomputed. The hold sits in the manager rather than the scheduler because peers' lookups reach `lookup()` without going through the scheduler.
- At reset, if any job is in flight, the scheduler records, for every flushed job, the worker reports still due (`pending_count`, so reports received before the reset count). Stale reports decrement it as they arrive, and the last one calls `on_reset_flushed()`; with nothing in flight it is called right away. The reports normally arrive within a step or two of the reset, so the cost is a short window without promotions.
- `has_pending_push_work()` also returns true while the scheduler waits for those reports. The reset clears `_jobs`, so without this an engine left with no request went idle before the flush reached the workers, and promotions (including peers' lookups) stayed held until unrelated work arrived.

**Limitations.** A worker that never reports its flushed jobs keeps promotions held; the warning makes that visible.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs (`reset_cache offloading`, `offload promotion reset`, `TieringOffloadingManager reset_cache`, `hold promotions offload`). None holds promotions across a reset. The closest are complementary:

- #59099 keeps the engine stepping until a reset's flush reaches the workers and makes `reset_cache()` re-entrant. This PR keeps the engine stepping only until the flushed jobs report; #59099 also covers engines without secondary tiers. A second reset before they report adds its own flushed jobs to the wait.
- #61667 quarantines `p2p` consumer slots whose remote write is unconfirmed. It covers a secondary tier's own late write, not a worker's.

**Related.** The multi-node CPU-region mirror proposed in #54415 (#62933) adds a second late writer, a remote node's pending slot push, and relies on this hook to cover it.

**AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, its tests and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Preserve fp16 in legacy fused MoE LoRA
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #59920. Preserve the input dtype in the legacy fused MoE LoRA GEMM instead of unconditionally converting operands to bfloat16.

## Claims
 Prevents silent fp16-to-bfloat16 conversion in the legacy shrink/expand kernel.
Keeps both Triton descriptor and pointer-load paths aligned with the hidden-state input dtype.
Extends large-rank fallback correctness coverage to fp16 and bf16.

## Validation

 `uv run --no-sync ruff check vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py`
 `uv run --no-sync ruff format --check ...`
 `uv run --no-sync python -m compileall -q vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py`
 The focused Triton test collection/execution could not run in this Windows CPU-only environment: vLLM native extension and `uvloop` are unavailable. CI or an Intel/NVIDIA/AMD GPU runner must execute `tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py`.
 No kernel benchmark was claimed; this is a correctness fix.

## Details

The legacy two-kernel path previously cast both dot operands to `tl.bfloat16` to work around ROCm type inference across TMA and pointer-load branches. That changes fp16 LoRA arithmetic and can produce incorrect outputs. The kernel now derives the dot dtype from the input pointer element type and casts both operands to that type. The large-rank fallback test is parameterized over the existing fp16 and bf16 dtype matrix.

## Overview

DeepSeek V4 / V4.1 MXFP4 experts now declare MXFP8 activations, the format they target on Blackwell. On Hopper, Humming runs a checkpoint-declared MXFP8 key as block FP8 (group 128), where its SM90 W4A8 kernels are tuned, instead of BF16. | | decode, output tok/s | 5039 / 5199 | 6237 / 6224 | +21% (TPOT 24.1 -> 19.7 ms) |
| | prefill, total tok/s | 29257 / 29421 | 30743 / 30835 | +5% |
| | low conc, output tok/s | 442.4 / 445.5 | 415.2 / 414.6 | -6.5% (TPOT 8.36 -> 8.98 ms) |

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 [--enable-expert-parallel] --max-model-len 16384
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 256
```

Tests: `pytest tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py` (11 passed; the new cases fail without the change) and `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_kernel_oracle.py`.

## Details

- `deepseek_v4` and `deepseek_v41` quant configs pass `activation_key=kMxfp8Dynamic` to `Mxfp4MoEMethod`. Before this, they passed no key, and Humming built its input schema from `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG`, which defaults to BF16.

- DeepSeek-V4's own checkpoint config describes block-128 UE8M0 FP8, while V4.1's is MXFP8-style (block 32). Both declare MXFP8 here, the Blackwell format; on Hopper both run as block FP8.
- DeepSeek-V4.1, DeepEP v2, and H100/H20 were not measured.
- The ROCm DeepSeek V4 path builds its own MoE method and is unaffected.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Release consumed MRV2 CPU inputs
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Release consumed request-local CPU multimodal payloads from MRV2 workers while requests are still decoding. This extends #52041's prefix-hit stripping to inputs that actually reached a worker, while retaining EngineCore replay data and GPU embeddings.

## Claims

- Release each occurrence only after its placeholder range is confirmed consumed; exclude in-flight prefill, unconfirmed output placeholders and inputs being encoded in the same step.
- Restore payloads when KV-load rollback schedules encoding again, including inputs initially stripped by a prefix hit. Preemption and streaming request installation rebuild tracking.
- Keep SHM processor-cache descriptors on their existing ACK protocol. MRV1 and encoder embedding eviction are unchanged.

## Validation

Code baseline: `2f1041e8dd05415d9984d0a83ad957d54a049eb4`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Focused scheduler regressions | 8 passed |
| Entire `test_encoder_runner.py` | 25 passed |
| Qwen3-VL live-generation regression, unchanged main | Fails: worker still holds the image payload after three steps while the request is alive |
| Same real-model regression, this patch | Passes: payload released, request completes 16 output tokens |
| Changed-file pre-commit, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX and CI tethering | Passed |
| `git diff --check` | Passed |

CPU commands:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/core tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k cpu_encoder_input -q
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/worker tests/v1/worker/test_encoder_runner.py -q
```

`--confcutdir` is only for the local macOS environment. Expanded scheduler/output testing had the same two unrelated failures on both arms: missing root `caplog_vllm` fixture and the local no-Triton fallback rejecting async MRV1+PP. The original main had 255 passes; the initial patch had 260 passes, and the three subsequent parameter cases passed separately.

Real-model reproducer on one H200:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_memory_leak.py -k consumed_cpu_inputs -v -s
```

Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`, greedy, eager. Both arms used Torch 2.14.0, Transformers 5.20.2 and FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1. The native wheel is `921ed7fa1`; its only difference from the tested main is `recipes/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.yaml`, so runtime and native sources match. `VLLM_MODEL_REDIRECT_PATH` pointed the existing model name at the local weight snapshot.

The GPU regression uses the real LLM entry point and the worker's actual EncoderCache, and is selected by the existing Multimodal Models Standard 4 job. Scheduler regressions exercise real constructors, scheduled outputs, forced preemption and invalid-block rollback. Worker tests verify storage reclamation, independent ownership and restored inputs reaching `EncoderRunner.prepare_mm_inputs`.

TP=2 integration checks also used Qwen3-VL on physical H200 GPUs 2/3, with the tensor arena enabled, processor caching disabled, prefix caching enabled, and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`:

| Live request at step 4 | Main | This patch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1024px image, below the arena threshold | Both workers retain approximately 6 MiB of inputs | Both workers drop their inputs |
| 1536px image, confirmed arena allocation | Both workers retain approximately 13.5 MiB; slot readers remain unacknowledged | Both workers drop their inputs; a fully acknowledged, reusable slot is observed before request completion |

Each arm completed a first request and a repeated-prefix request with 32 output tokens each. Token IDs matched exactly across main/patch in both image-size cases; cancellation cleared request-local cache entries. These are small deterministic comparisons, not a full quality evaluation. Slot snapshots are asynchronous; the memory figures describe each worker's payload references, not additive physical-memory savings. Cancellation may still leave short-lived references outside EncoderCache.

The node could not initialize NVLS multicast, including on main; both TP2 arms ran with `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0`. Existing fallback all-reduce paths were used without changing vLLM code. No GPU synchronization error was raised. Physical GPUs 4/5 were excluded throughout.

Current-revision host-memory A/B (Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, MRV2, TP=2, physical H200 GPUs 0/2): 16 distinct 1536px image requests arriving in two waves of 8, each generating 128 tokens. Each configuration/arm had two independent engine starts with reversed arm order on the second start, one warmup and three formal rounds per start. PSS sums the driver/EngineCore and its worker process tree, avoiding shared-page double counting. Means below use snapshots with all 16 requests alive and each having generated at least 8, 32 and 64 tokens.

| Configuration | Main decode PSS | Patch decode PSS | Reduction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default 4 GiB LRU processor cache, arena off | 6.950 GiB | 6.567 GiB | 393.0 MiB / 5.52% |
| Processor cache off, arena off | 6.733 GiB | 6.303 GiB | 440.7 MiB / 6.39% |
| Processor cache off, arena on | 8.493 GiB | 8.131 GiB | 370.1 MiB / 4.26% |

Worker request-cache input references fell from approximately 216 MiB per rank to zero in all cases. With the arena enabled, slot-exhaustion fallbacks fell from 8 to 0 per round; all 8 slots became reusable while requests were still alive. The arena's 2 GiB pinned mapping remains allocated, so this is slot reuse, not unmapping the arena. In this small workload, the arena's fixed mapping also makes its absolute PSS larger than the arena-off configuration.

Corresponding output token IDs matched for all 576 formal requests across the three configurations, with 128 tokens per request. The two independent-start PSS reductions with default LRU caching were 402.0 and 383.9 MiB. These are workload-specific decode-residency measurements, not universal percentages or exact prefill peaks. The driver and EngineCore share a process in this harness; workers use the real multiprocess TP executor. Configuration: eager, max model length 4096, batched tokens 2048, sequences 16, GPU memory utilization 0.20, seed 0, prefix caching enabled with distinct inputs, NVLS disabled equally on both arms, and GPU sync checking enabled. No allocator trimming or production-code instrumentation was used. EngineCore replay inputs and its LRU cache are still retained.

No throughput speedup or full accuracy result is claimed for this revision. KV-load failure restoration is covered by CPU scheduler/worker tests, not a distributed KV-transfer model run.

## Details

A single `SchedulerOutput.encoder_input_updates` map carries payload replacement by request ID and input index: `None` releases an input; a payload restores it. An index has one update per step, avoiding separate restore/free ordering. The scheduler tracks only remaining releasable inputs and stops scanning once none remain.

Workers apply updates after request installation and RoPE position initialization. Replacing entries in a worker-owned list preserves EngineCore's original feature objects, including with the uniprocess executor. The same placeholder metadata remains available for embedding gathering and PrefixLM ranges.

Related work and scope:

- #52041/#53456 handle stripping before initial position computation. This patch releases after that initialization and does not change their metadata rules.
- #54994 preserves SHM address references; those descriptors remain excluded here.
- #51207 shares transport storage. It does not release request-local references, and its slots cannot be reused until their storage references are dropped. This PR adds no COW or other transport.
- #62834 checks remote encoder embedding readiness during EPD replay; it does not restore a local worker's raw inputs for re-encoding.
- Open #50871 clears EngineCore inputs for resumable sessions. This patch requires retained EngineCore payloads for rollback; combining the two requires an explicit replay policy.
- #56813 caches position ranges, which this patch does not change; #56826/#62850 optimize other cache cleanup. None implements this running-request payload lifecycle.

No user-facing configuration or behavior contract is added, so no separate design document is introduced. AI assistance was used for implementation, upstream comparison, review and validation.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Preserve new loads during same-step resume
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix an OffloadingConnector assertion when a prefix-cache reset preempts a request and its next scheduling step both reports that preemption and creates a new KV load. Exclude only loads created in the current step from the preemption flush, while preserving the store-only check for older jobs.

Related to the serving path exercised by #60552. This deliberately overlaps the same-step resume fix in #57810; the scope and implementation differences are described below.

## Claims

- Preserve newly created CPU-to-GPU loads through the preemption notification, allowing the request to resume and finish.
- Continue flushing earlier stores and checking their transfer type before block reuse.

## Validation

Standalone patch on `0f112d180033f3757cf283723f5593a40b02ed82`:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  -k 'preempt or reset' -v
```

**10 passed.** Pre-commit passed for both changed files.

The two new cases reproduce the assertion before the fix in both synchronous and asynchronous scheduling. They start with a running request and no pending transfers, then verify that its new load is not flushed, completes normally, and the resumed request finishes. Existing cases cover preemption with pending stores and explicit connector reset.

Combined serving validation on the same base, with this patch and the separate #60552 return-value fix applied: one RTX 3070, Qwen3-0.6B, eager execution with `TRITON_ATTN`, 320 GPU blocks and 4 GB CPU offload. The Python checkout reused the official v0.31.0+cu129 CUDA extensions.

- Strict replay, using `ignore_eos=True` and streamed usage checks: 3 flagged and 3 control resets returned `200 {"success": false}`; all 12 streams completed 64 tokens, all 6 follow-up health/generation checks passed, and every trial recorded positive offload-load bytes.
- The original #60552 client then completed 5 flagged and 5 control trials on the same server, all HTTP 200 and healthy, without the connector assertion.

These are combined-patch serving results. This PR does not change the HTTP reset failure contract; the standalone regression coverage is reported separately above.

No model-quality or performance claim is made. The serving checks validate HTTP responses, stream completion and continued generation; upstream CI has not been run for this proposed PR.

## Details

`reset_prefix_cache()` queues a preemption notification for the next `schedule()`. That step may already create a load to restore the same request from the offloaded cache. The preemption flush incorrectly assumes every pending transfer predates the preemption and must be a store, so it asserts on the new load.

Subtract `self._current_batch_load_jobs.keys()` only when collecting jobs for the preemption flush. These loads have not yet been submitted to the worker; they remain in the load metadata and retain their normal completion and cleanup path. Older jobs still pass through the existing assertion and flush logic.

**Overlap with #57810:** that open PR already fixes the same root cause as part of its pause/sleep cache-retention feature. This is proposed as a small standalone alternative because the crash is reproducible on current main without that feature. Unlike filtering all pending jobs by `is_store`, this version excludes only current-step loads and retains the assertion for older jobs. It introduces no cache-retention option or pause/sleep API changes. Author/maintainer coordination is pending; the overlapping fix should be consolidated into one implementation rather than merged twice.

Developed and validated with OpenAI Codex assistance.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Mark the session dead when its ConnectAck send fails
commits.pr_body:
## Overview `P2PSession._poll_registration` clears the pending registration before sending `ConnectAckMsg`. If that send raises, the exception escapes `poll()` and the local session remains alive. Route the ack through `_do_send` so a send exception marks the local connection dead and allows the manager to reap its pending work. Part of #63602 (gap 5). ## Claims - A raised `ConnectAckMsg` send error marks the local connection dead instead of escaping `poll()`. - The manager can reap that session and fail its pending local work without waiting for the request deadline, provided polling and cleanup can progress. - The ack still bypasses the pre-ack queue. Successful sends also refresh the session's activity timestamp. - This does not guarantee immediate remote notification or bound a blocking transport send. ## Validation New test `TestConnectHandshake::test_failed_ack_send_marks_connection_dead` (`tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py`): a peer's registration completes, the ack send raises, and the connection must be dead after `poll()`. The existing `test_sessions.py::TestDisconnect::test_send_failure_marks_connection_dead` covers send-error handling. The existing `test_manager.py::TestConnectionDeathMidTransfer::test_dead_connection_with_pending_work_surfaces_failures` covers failure of a dead session's pending load, and separately asserts that an unbound store stays parked for its own timeout. Neither is an end-to-end failed-ack-send test. Run on CPU in `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:cb9bc64f0f038c2c2ebf13b31248fb87aca40c356c3d20f363be087cfcff1fcd` with this tree mounted (`uv venv --system-site-packages`, then `pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p`): ``` # new test, against the base commit's session.py E ConnectionError: simulated dead connection FAILED tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py::TestConnectHandshake::test_failed_ack_send_marks_connection_dead 1 failed # new test, with this change 1 passed # the two existing dead-connection tests above, with this change 2 passed # full P2P suite (tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p), with this change FAILED tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py::TestBidirectionalManager::test_lookup_expiry_allows_zmq_reconnect 1 failed, 311 passed ``` `test_lookup_expiry_allows_zmq_reconnect` also fails on the unmodified base. Run alone, alternating between the base and this change in one CPU container, it failed 16 of 20 times on each, always in the `poll_until(both_ready)` after the reconnect (`test_manager.py:1341`); no difference was observed in this sample. The failing full-suite run with this change contains no `send of connect_ack failed` warning, so the ack-send exception handler was not observed; successful acks still go through the changed direct-send path. Its cause is unresolved. Integration check on GPUs of this change together with a rollback patch for gap 4 (not part of this PR; gap 4 is handled in #63628), #63207 and #63498, on nightly `8e2beaa3b`: three single-GPU Qwen3-0.6B engines on one H200 node, mlx5 InfiniBand, NIXL 1.5.0, 1 run per case. A probe seeds a fresh ~2K-token prefix on a source every 200 ms and asks consumer A to pull it. A probe counts as pulled when A submitted the P2P load and the source logged `finalize ... success=True ... send_done=True` for it. Times run from SIGCONT, or from the switch to the replacement pod, to the HTTP request start and finish of the first such probe: | fault on source B | probes to B or its replacement pulled after recovery | first verified pull after recovery, request start / finish | probes to healthy source C pulled | |---|---|---|---| | none | 700/700 | - | 625/625 | | SIGSTOP 60 s, then SIGCONT | 242/242 (from SIGCONT + 40 s) | 8.7 s / 10.1 s | 616/616 | | pod force-deleted, replacement | 400/400 (from switch + 10 s) | 0.5 s / 0.8 s | 848/848 | | pod deleted gracefully, replacement | 400/400 (from switch + 10 s) | 0.3 s / 0.5 s | 839/839 | Every successful handshake in these runs sent its ack through `_do_send`. The runs do not establish that the ack-send exception handler was exercised; they check that the combined stack does not regress. No `LLM`/`RemoteOpenAIServer` fault-injection regression is included. The fault is injected at the external transport boundary in the focused tests above. We have not implemented an entry-point fixture for this failure; asking maintainers to accept this test scope. ## Details `_do_send` is the existing guarded direct-send path. commits.pr_title: [Metrics][KV Offload] Fill vllm:kv_offload_config_info with the CPU cache capacity
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

GPU KV-cache capacity is observable. `num_gpu_blocks` and `kv_cache_size_tokens`
are labels on `vllm:cache_config_info`. The CPU offload tier exports only usage
(`vllm:kv_offload_cpu_cache_usage_perc` and the read/write variants) and no
capacity. The size is not recoverable externally either, because it depends on
`blocks_per_chunk`, page alignment, and whether a replicated layout deduplicates
the per-worker copies. All three are connector-internal.

This PR fills `vllm:kv_offload_config_info` with the CPU cache facts. The gauge,
the label rendering and the emission call come from #56867, the generic
config-info PR. The CPU side adds four labels:

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `cpu_num_chunks` | Chunk slots in the tier. Chunks, not GPU blocks. |
| `cpu_blocks_per_chunk` | GPU blocks in one chunk: the chunk-to-block conversion factor. |
| `cpu_kv_cache_size_bytes` | Size of the tier in bytes: `cpu_num_chunks` times the page-aligned bytes of one chunk. |
| `cpu_kv_cache_size_tokens` | KV tokens the tier holds for requests of `max_model_len` tokens. It is computed like the GPU `kv_cache_size_tokens`. |

No name carries a tier index, so a CPU fact reads the same under
`CPUOffloadingSpec` and under `TieringOffloadingSpec`. The gauge is per engine.
Sum across the `engine` label for the instance total. The Info shape is the
extensible container the reviewers of #49307 asked for.

### `cpu_kv_cache_size_tokens`

The tier is content-addressed (`OffloadKey = block_hash + group_idx`), so there is
no per-request allocation to divide by, and no analogue of the GPU
`max_concurrency`. The token capacity depends on the request length. The label
fixes the length at `max_model_len`, as the GPU `kv_cache_size_tokens` does:

```
chunks_per_request       = sum over groups of min(cdiv(max_model_len, tokens_per_chunk), cap)
cpu_kv_cache_size_tokens = num_chunks * max_model_len // chunks_per_request
```

Both `tokens_per_chunk` and `cap` are per group. `tokens_per_chunk` is
`blocks_per_chunk * tokens_per_block` of that group. `cap` is the chunks of that
group the tier keeps for one request: `None` for attention that reaches back
without a bound, `cdiv(window, tokens_per_chunk)` for a sliding window, and 1 for
Mamba. A capped group holds a fixed number of chunks however long the request
grows.

Two values cross the `OffloadingConfig` boundary for this:
`OffloadingGroupConfig.sliding_window_size_in_chunks` and
`OffloadingModelConfig.max_model_len`. `build_offloading_config` computes the first
one with `get_sliding_window_size_in_chunks`. The connector scheduler now reads the
same field, so the value has one source. Both new fields have a default, so a
spec that does not read them does not change.

`None` covers two cases: a `max_model_len` of 0, and no KV cache group at all. Zero
chunks reports `0`, not `None`, because zero slots hold exactly zero tokens.

`CPUOffloadingInfo.from_config(config, num_chunks, kv_bytes_per_chunk)` builds the
labels. The CPU spec builds it once as `cpu_info`, and passes it to the manager
as the last keyword argument `info`. `TieringOffloadingSpec` inherits `cpu_info`
and passes it to its primary tier.

### Why this estimate

The GPU side answers the same question in the same three steps.
`get_kv_cache_capacity` (`kv_cache_utils.py:2291`) builds `kv_cache_size_tokens`
like this:

```
num_blocks_per_request = sum over groups of cdiv(max_memory_usage_bytes, page_size_bytes)
max_concurrency        = num_blocks / num_blocks_per_request
kv_cache_size_tokens   = int(max_concurrency * max_model_len)
```

Sum the per-request cost over the groups, divide the pool by that sum, multiply by
the request length. The formula above does the same, with chunks in place of blocks.

The per-group cap matches too. `SlidingWindowSpec.max_memory_usage_bytes` calls
`max_admission_blocks_per_request`, which bounds a windowed group by its window
(`kv_cache_interface.py:716`). `MambaSpec.max_memory_usage_bytes` charges one page
for each request in the default cache mode (`kv_cache_interface.py:922`).

Both numbers report an upper bound, because both assume that every request reaches
`max_model_len`. An operator reads the two side by side.

### Worked examples

Every number below is pinned in `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_capacity.py`.
`held` is `min(cdiv(max_model_len, tokens_per_chunk), cap)`.

**Qwen3-8B**, TP 2, 1 full group, `tokens_per_chunk` 256, 4500 slots,
`max_model_len` 36864: `chunks_per_request = 144`, and `4500 * 36864 // 144 = 1152000`.

**gemma-3-27b-it**, TP 2, 1 full group and 6 sliding-window groups, window 1024
tokens, so `cap` is 4. `tokens_per_chunk` 256, 4000 slots, `max_model_len` 36864:

| Groups | cap | cdiv(36864, 256) | held | subtotal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 full | None | 144 | 144 | 144 |
| 6 SWA | 4 | 144 | 4 | 24 |

`chunks_per_request = 168`, and `4000 * 36864 // 168 = 877714`.

**granite-4.0-h-small**, TP 2, 1 full group and 9 Mamba groups, `tokens_per_chunk`
528, 8000 slots, `max_model_len` 36864:

| Groups | cap | cdiv(36864, 528) | held | subtotal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 full | None | 70 | 70 | 70 |
| 9 Mamba | 1 | 70 | 1 | 9 |

`chunks_per_request = 79`, and `8000 * 36864 // 79 = 3733063`.

**A hybrid with one group of each kind**, `tokens_per_chunk` 256, 4000 slots,
`max_model_len` 36864, window 1024 tokens: `chunks_per_request = 144 + 4 + 1 = 149`,
and `4000 * 36864 // 149 = 989637`. If all three groups grew with the request, the
answer would be 341333. The caps carry most of the number on a hybrid model.

### Relation to #56867, #49307 and #51615

**#56867** adds `vllm:kv_offload_config_info` and the mechanism that fills it, with
no real value behind it. This PR supplies the CPU values. #56867 has landed
(`775fefa804`), and this branch is rebased on top of it through current `main`.

**#49307 (@yanburman)** became this same metric after review (@orozery: bundle
static tier information into one Info metric following `vllm:cache_config_info`),
emitted once at engine startup. That needed a new public `get_config_info()`
connector API, an `EngineCoreReadyResponse` field, a runtime-populated
`KVTransferConfig` side-channel and a `record_config_info()` chain. All of those
edit code outside `kv_offload/` and `offloading/`, which reviewers objected to.
**#51615 (@nilig, draft)** emits `vllm:kv_offload_cpu_capacity_tokens` through the
existing connector-stats path.

This PR takes the metric shape of #49307 and the emission mechanism of #51615. The
cost is that the metric is absent (no series, never `0`) until the first scheduler
step.

## Test Plan

- **Unit tests** - 15 new test functions, over four sections of the change.

    - **The capacity arithmetic** - `test_capacity.py` calls
      `CPUOffloadingInfo.from_config` and covers the four model shapes above, a
      pure-Mamba model, an empty tier, and the two cases with no token scale.
    - **The tier sizing** - the labels of a real `CPUOffloadingSpec` report the
      numbers the spec resolved, under tensor parallel, under a replicated
      layout, and with a second group that shares the slots.
    - **The config boundary** - `build_offloading_config` fills the two new
      fields, `sliding_window_size_in_chunks` on the group and `max_model_len` on
      the model.
    - **The tiering pass-through** - the primary tier reports the four labels
      on the `0:primary` series, the tiering spec gives it `cpu_info`, and the
      tiering spec declares exactly the names the manager fills.

    Files: `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_capacity.py` is new and holds 2 (11 cases).
    `tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py` holds 10,
    `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py` holds 2, and
    `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py` holds 1.
    `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py` gains no test. Its
    drift guard now pins the four CPU names next to the secondary tier names.
    `test_scheduler.py` only gives its mock group the new field.

    ```bash
    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload \
      tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector \
      --ignore=tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_offload_integrity.py -q
    ```

- **Lint** - `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`.

- **Documentation** - `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md` adds three rows to the
  "Info Metric Labels" table of #56867, one for each new label.

- **Model evaluations: not applicable.** Metrics only. The PR touches no scheduling,
  no KV-cache placement, no transfer behavior and no model output.

- **GPU and data-parallel sanity runs** - four servers on the pokprod cluster, one
  H100 80 GB per engine: the merge base and this branch with `Qwen3-8B` as an
  A/B pair, then this branch with `TieringOffloadingSpec` and the `example`
  secondary tier (`Qwen3-0.6B`), with `--data-parallel-size 2` (`Qwen3-0.6B`),
  and with `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, a model with sliding-window and full-attention
  layers. Each server answers 96 completion requests in three rounds.

- **Not verified.** A real hybrid Mamba model stays untested.

## Test Result

At `87e4b690cf`, on macOS (no CUDA, no `/dev/shm`):

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_config`, `test_factory`, `test_capacity`, `test_tiering_offloading`, `test_scheduler` | `626 passed, 1 skipped` |
| Full offload suites (command above) | `1341 passed, 86 failed, 16 skipped` |
| Same suites at the previous branch tip | `1353 passed, 86 failed, 16 skipped` |

- The same 86 tests fail before and after. All are in `cpu/test_gpu_worker.py` (32)
  and `cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py` (54), which need CUDA and `/dev/shm`.
- The pass count is 12 lower only because the PR removed the old capacity tests.
- `test_offload_integrity.py` is excluded. It cannot import `StoreTrigger`, which
  also fails without this PR's changes.
- The skipped test in `test_factory.py`
  (`test_tiering_spec_passes_the_cpu_facts_to_the_primary_tier`) needs `/dev/shm`,
  so it runs in CI.

**GPU runs**, on the pokprod cluster, one H100 80 GB per engine, at `87e4b690cf`.
The image is a nightly build of an ancestor of the merge base. The package tree
holds the exact merge-base checkout, and the branch files sit on top of it. A
server of the merge base runs as the control.

The control and this branch, `Qwen3-8B`, `cpu_bytes_to_use` of 10 GiB,
`blocks_per_chunk` of 4, `max_model_len` 8192: the same store counter
(44694503424 bytes), the same query counter (306541), the same round-3 texts

The labels, each equal to the value computed by hand from the model shape:

- Qwen3-8B: 2 × 2 bytes × 36 layers × 8 KV heads × 128 head dim × 16 tokens per

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Exclude rc_gda lanes from the P2P NIXL agent
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The P2P KV offload tier creates its NIXL UCX backend with UCX's default transports, which include the `rc_gda` GPU device lanes. After a P2P peer stalls or is replaced, connecting those lanes fails, so the peer was not usable again during the observation window (90 s): registering it fails, or its WRITEs stall, and every pull from it falls back to local prefill. This creates the tier's UCX backend with `engine_config="TLS=^rc_gda"`; the tier only moves host memory.

Fixes #63499.

Related: #63207 (the control-plane freeze in the same fault cases; without it the replacement cases freeze before reaching this bug), ai-dynamo/nixl#2437 / ai-dynamo/nixl#2337 (the `NIXL_ERR_INVALID_PARAM` loop that follows the first failed registration).

## Claims

- After a pause, the peer is pulled from again: the first pull succeeded 9-12 s after SIGCONT, and every probe from 40 s after SIGCONT on was pulled. After a replacement, the first pull came 0.3-0.7 s after the switch, and every probe from 10 s after the switch was pulled. Without the change, no pull from that peer completed during the observation window (90 s).
- No change for a healthy fleet, and none when `UCX_TLS` is set: UCX env vars take precedence over `engine_config`.

## Validation

Three single-GPU engines (Qwen3-0.6B, `--enforce-eager -O0`) on 8xH200 nodes with mlx5 InfiniBand: consumer A, source B that the fault hits, healthy source C. `OffloadingConnector` + `TieringOffloadingSpec`, 8 GiB CPU tier, P2P tier over RDMA, NIXL 1.5.0. Both arms run nightly `8e2beaa3b` + #63207 (`478d86b21`); the change is the only difference. A probe seeds a fresh ~2K-token prefix on B or C every 200 ms and asks A to pull it (`kv_transfer_params.remote_kv_source`); "recovered" means A's requests to B (or B2) after recovery were pulled (A logged `request_blocks ... blocks>0` for them).

| fault on B | without this change | with this change |
|---|---|---|
| none | pass 1/1 | pass 1/1 |
| SIGSTOP 60 s, then SIGCONT | no pull in 90 s, 0/3 | recovers, 2/2: first pull 9-12 s after SIGCONT; every probe pulled from SIGCONT + 40 s (p50 0.051-0.057 s) |
| pod deleted gracefully, replacement B2 | no completed pull from B2 in 90 s, 0/3 (35-36 requested per run, none completed) | recovers, 2/2: first pull 0.7 s after the switch; 400/400 from switch + 10 s (p50 0.056-0.057 s) |
| pod force-deleted, replacement B2 | recovers 1/3 (no pull from B2 in 90 s in the other two) | recovers, 2/2: first pull 0.6-0.7 s after the switch; 400/400 from switch + 10 s (p50 0.053-0.058 s) |
| SIGSTOP, B on another node | no pull in 90 s, 0/1 | recovers, 1/1: first pull 10.6 s after SIGCONT; 242/242 from SIGCONT + 40 s |
| graceful replacement, B2 on another node | no pull from B2 in 90 s, 0/2 | recovers, 1/1: first pull 0.3 s after the switch; 400/400 from switch + 10 s |

Across nodes, the graceful replacement fails through registration (`REMOTE_DISCONNECT`, then `INVALID_PARAM`) rather than the WRITE stall seen on one node. With NIXL main + ai-dynamo/nixl#2337 (and UCX v1.23.x) the `INVALID_PARAM` loop is gone, but recovery still fails: registration retries fail with `REMOTE_DISCONNECT` in the pause and force-delete cases, and 35-39 WRITEs stall in the graceful-replacement case. With `UCX_TLS=tcp,self,cuda_copy` all three recover (5/5); with `UCX_TLS=^rc_gda` set in the environment all three recover (3/3), matching this change.

Unit tests (`tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p`, CPU):

```
# this change
311 passed
# updated agent-config tests against main's nixl.py
FAILED test_data_transport.py::TestNixlAgentConfigSelection::test_ucx_only_creates_backend_without_rc_gda
FAILED test_data_transport.py::TestNixlAgentConfigSelection::test_default_backends_is_ucx_only
2 failed, 1 passed
```

CI cannot reproduce the failure: it needs RDMA NICs, GPUs and a peer fault between two engines. The updated tests only pin the backend configuration.

## Details

With UCX's GPU device API (NIXL sets `UCP_FEATURE_DEVICE`), every UCX endpoint gets `rc_gda` lanes next to its `rc_mlx5` lanes, whether or not GPU memory is ever transferred. UCX debug logs on the consumer for the SIGSTOP case:

1. At t+31 s (B stopped at t+21 s) the P2P session drops B and NIXL closes the endpoint; UCX destroys it after the UD keepalive times out at t+62 s.
2. B resumes at t+81 s and the session re-registers it at t+91 s: the new endpoint connects all eight `rc_mlx5` lanes, then the next lane connect fails:
   ```
   ib_mlx5_dv.c:446  UCX  ERROR   mlx5dv_devx_obj_modify(opcode=0x503) failed, syndrome 0x5d668c: Remote I/O error
   ucp_ep.c:1621 UCX  DEBUG ep 0x...: set_ep_failed status Input/output error
   nixl_agent.cpp:1679] loadRemoteMD: error loading remote metadata for agent '<B>' with status NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT
   P2PSession <B>: peer registration failed, rejecting peer: NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT
   ```
3. On NIXL 1.5.0 every later registration of B then fails with `NIXL_ERR_INVALID_PARAM` (ai-dynamo/nixl#2437). With NIXL main + #2337 the retries fail with `REMOTE_DISCONNECT` instead.

In the graceful-replacement case on one node, registration succeeds, but B2's WRITEs to A do not complete during the run and report no error; the stalled transfers pin CPU-tier chunks on both sides until both report `cannot store chunks`, which also drops some pulls from the healthy C (679/847 pulled). Excluding `rc_gda` removes that form as well.

The tier registers and transfers DRAM only, so it never uses the device lanes; dropping them also removes four lanes per endpoint. The change follows the `engine_config` mechanism the NIXL connector uses for its sleep-mode agent. On UCX versions without `rc_gda`, an unknown name in a negated `TLS` list is ignored without a warning. The underlying UCX failure (an `rc_gda` connect rejected after a peer fault) is not addressed here.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Match the DeepSeek-V4.1 FP8 config in the shared-expert FSE compatibility check
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On CUDA and ROCm, `deepseek_v4_fp8` always resolves to the DeepSeek-V4.1 `DeepseekV4FP8Config`, which subclasses `Fp8Config`, not the V4 class. `is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible` runs its DeepSeek-V4 checks only for the V4 class, so on these platforms it falls through to the generic `Fp8Config` branch and reports every DeepSeek-V4 shared expert as FSE-compatible. This PR matches both classes for MXFP4 routed experts, as the online-quantization branch of the same function already does.

Founded by Hyperloom.

## Claims

- Fixes the weight-loading failure of DeepSeek-V4-Flash on ROCm with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`. Quark MXFP4 checkpoints hit the same failure on the FP8 MTP shared expert.
- No change when the variable is unset: the check is not called.
- No change for FP8-expert checkpoints such as DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base: they keep the generic FP8 check, as on main.
- Adds `test_deepseek_v41_quant_config_rejects_fp8_mtp_shared_expert_fse` and `test_deepseek_v41_fp8_experts_keep_fp8_fse_check`.

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950), `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, TP1, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256`, vLLM built from main at 15a78aa88e (the touched files are unchanged on current main).

With `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`, main fails during weight loading in 2 of 2 runs:

```
KeyError: 'layers.0.ffn.experts.routed_experts.w13_weight_scale_inv'
```

With this PR, all 43 layers reject FSE ("only implemented/tested with Quark MXFP4"), run the shared expert unfused, and serve.

|---|---|---|---|
| main, variable unset | 10061 (±3.5%) | 1026 | 24.68 |
| this PR, variable unset | 10033 (±0.8%) | 1024 | 24.76 |
| this PR, variable = 1 | 10045 (±0.2%) | 1027 | 24.77 |

GSM8K, 5-shot, greedy, 1319 items, `lm_eval --model local-completions`:

| Arm | strict-match | Same verdict as main |
|---|---|---|
| main | 0.9515 ± 0.0059 | - |
