commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Do not store sliding-window chunks with null blocks
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Fixes #63653. With offloaded chunks of several GPU blocks, `OffloadingConnector` could store a sliding-window chunk that contained a null block. A later CPU hit then loaded the never-written slot as KV, and the request's output changed with no error. ## Claims - A sliding-window chunk is stored only when every block that the store mask marks reachable is present, so a CPU hit no longer loads a slot that no store wrote. - One-block chunks and full-attention groups behave as before. A one-block chunk with a null block was already skipped, and full-attention block tables hold no null blocks. ## Validation Two new tests: - `test_sliding_window_chunk_with_null_block_is_not_stored` in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py`: scheduler level, sync and async scheduling. - `test_cpu_offloading_sliding_window_partial_chunk` in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py`: LLM level, CUDA, `google/gemma-3-1b-it` with `blocks_per_chunk=8` and `store_threshold=2`. Request B's GPU hit ends mid-chunk, which leaves null sliding-window blocks inside chunk 0, and B stores that chunk. The test asserts that this hit length is reached, so the case is exercised, and that a request hitting the chunk on the CPU tier produces the same output as a cold run. Scheduler-level test without the fix (main `24324ef0`), failing at the store check for request B: ``` $ pytest --tb=short -q "tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py::test_sliding_window_chunk_with_null_block_is_not_stored" tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py:2299: in test_sliding_window_chunk_with_null_block_is_not_stored tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/utils.py:680: in run E AssertionError FAILED ...::test_sliding_window_chunk_with_null_block_is_not_stored[True] FAILED ...::test_sliding_window_chunk_with_null_block_is_not_stored[False] 2 failed in 1.11s ``` Line 2299 is `runner.run(decoded_tokens=[EOS_TOKEN_ID], expected_stored=((0, 0), (0, 1)))`: on main, B also stores sliding-window block 1 without block 0. With the fix, `2 passed in 1.29s`. LLM-level test: not run on a GPU, because I don't have one. CI runs it on CUDA. I ran its helper `_sliding_window_partial_chunk_test` on CPU against a tiny random Gemma-3 (512-token window, GPU block 32, 8 blocks per chunk). The offload copy was done by an out-of-tree spec that runs `gpu_worker.py`'s transfer code with `memmove` in place of the CUDA kernel (described in the linked issue). - On main it fails at `assert out_c.outputs[0].token_ids == cold_c.outputs[0].token_ids`: C's greedy tokens change, and C loaded 114,688 bytes that no store wrote. - With the fix it passes, and C loads nothing. End to end on CPU with the same spec, comparing C's output against a run without offloading: | Run | C's CPU hit | Loaded bytes no store wrote | C's logprobs vs no offloading | |---|---|---|---| | main, 64-token window, 2 blocks per chunk | 64 tokens | 16,384 | off by 0.11 to 0.15 at every step | | main, chunk-aligned control | 64 tokens | 0 | identical | | main, 512-token window, 8 blocks per chunk | 512 tokens | 114,688 (7 blocks) | off by 0.18 to 0.39; 3 of the top-5 first tokens change | | this PR, both shapes | none (recomputed) | 0 | identical | Model evaluation: the fix changes only which chunks get stored, so an affected request recomputes a chunk instead of loading it. An accuracy benchmark wouldn't isolate the bug, because the bug needs a specific hit-then-evict pattern. The runs above construct that pattern and compare against a run without offloading. The LLM-level test does the same in CI against a cold run on `google/gemma-3-1b-it`. Suites, run with `pytest -q ` on CPU (macOS arm64, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`) at `24324ef0`: | Suite | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/` | 628 passed, 2 skipped | 630 passed, 2 skipped | | `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py` | 2 failed, 3 skipped | 2 failed, 4 skipped (the same 2 failures) | | `tests/v1/core` | 1059 passed, 1 failed, 4 errors | the same counts and the same failing tests | | `tests/v1/kv_offload` (without `cpu/test_gpu_worker.py`) | 718 passed, 54 failed, 10 skipped | the same counts and the same failing tests | The failures on both sides are environment limits on this Mac: - the two tiering tests download a gated model; - in `tests/v1/core`, the hybrid test model needs `causal_conv1d_weight_pack`, which the CPU build lacks, and one test's block size is unsupported; - the `kv_offload` failures are `cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py`, which needs `/dev/shm`. `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files passes, including ruff 0.14.0, typos, mypy and the Buildkite test-wiring check. The branch merges cleanly into main `237d2ffd`. On that merge, the scheduler-level test, the LLM-level helper on CPU and the `offloading_connector` suite (632 passed, 2 skipped) all pass. ## Details Root cause, with lines at `24324ef0`: - A GPU prefix-cache hit leaves sliding-window blocks before the window null (`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1004-1037`). A sliding-window free also zeroes pending store positions (`offloading/scheduler.py:1503-1522`). - With the default `prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`, a GPU hit lands on an earlier prompt's replay boundary. That boundary is block-aligned but not necessarily chunk-aligned, so the null run can end mid-chunk. - `_build_store_jobs` selected chunks by their last block only (`offloading/scheduler.py:1880-1891`, `1917`), then dropped null blocks from the store spec (`1995`). - The worker wrote part of the chunk (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py:635-654`), while `complete_store` marked all of it ready (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/manager.py:370-387`). The fix adds one check to key selection. After the existing reachability test, a chunk is skipped if any block the store mask marks reachable is null. With no mask, any null block skips it. No GPU block exists to copy for that position, so the chunk can't be completed. A later request that would have hit this chunk computes it instead: it loses a partial CPU hit and avoids loading stale KV. Null blocks that the mask marks unreachable are still allowed. A request whose window excludes them holds null blocks there too, and its load skips those slots. Test changes: - `RequestRunner` rejected `blocks_per_chunk > 1` whenever custom KV cache groups were passed. It now accepts them when every group uses the runner's block size. - `_wait_for_prefix_cache_reset` takes `reset_connector`, so the LLM-level test can clear the CPU tier before its cold run. Not a duplicate: as of 2026-10-26, no open or closed issue or PR reports this bug. I ran 20 keyword searches over issues and PRs and checked the 171 open PRs that touch the offloading connector or `kv_offload/`. The closest are these two: - #57216 guards the end-of-request partial-chunk store against null blocks. This PR covers full chunks. - Draft #61426 moves this loop into `store_triggers/on_compute.py` and keeps the last-block check. If it lands first, this check goes there. AI assistance: Claude (Anthropic) found this bug with a randomized checker over the offloading connector. It also wrote the reproductions, the CPU end-to-end harness, both tests and the fix, and ran the suites above. I reviewed every changed line and reran the tests and the CPU end-to-end check. The commit carries a `Co-authored-by` trailer. ---

commits.pr_title: [KV Offload] Load small CPU-tier hits synchronously within the step
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On wide-EP MoE prefill (such as GLM-5.3), a step takes 0.3 to 0.5 s. Almost every request has a small CPU-tier hit, and an async load parks it for about 2 steps although the copy takes ~1 ms.

This adds an opt-in `sync_load_budget_bytes` option (`kv_connector_extra_config`, default 0, off): small hits load in the same step, up to that many KV bytes per GPU per step. The change stays in the offloading connector, the `OffloadingWorker` interface, and the CPU offloading worker.

## Changes

- `scheduler.py`: a hit that fits the step's remaining budget returns `load_async=False`, so the request is scheduled in this step; the load targets its blocks by position and is marked sync. `_current_batch_sync_loads` and the byte total reset every step.
- `worker.py`: submits sync loads with `submit_load(..., expedited=True)`, waits for them before the forward pass, and does not report them in `finished_recving`.
- `kv_offload/base.py`, `cpu/gpu_worker.py`: an `expedited` flag on `OffloadingWorker.submit_load`; the CPU worker runs expedited loads on their own stream.
- `common.py`: a `TransferJob.sync` flag carries that decision from scheduler to worker.

## Claims

- Small hits load in the same step, up to `sync_load_budget_bytes` of KV per GPU per step; the rest stay async. The budget exists because the whole batch waits for the copy. A hit that would leave nothing to compute stays async.
- Sync-load blocks are hashed at allocation, so the load range is found by position. Other requests can match them in the same step, which is safe since the forward pass waits for the copy.
- Sync loads use their own stream, so they never wait behind async loads.
- With the option at 0, behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

Qwen3-30B-A3B on H100, OffloadingConnector + TieringOffloadingSpec. 12k-token prefix in GPU cache, 2k-token tail only in the CPU tier. Median extra TTFT vs a GPU-hit control:

| Setup | Without fix | With fix (limit 4096) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 node: DP=2 + EP (this version, 10 reps) | +219 ms | +1 ms |
| 2 nodes: TP=8, DP=2, EP over 16 GPUs (12 reps) | +344 ms | +8 ms |

These numbers were measured with the earlier per-request token limit (`sync_load_max_tokens=4096`) and a shared load stream; the per-step byte budget and separate stream are not yet run end to end.

GLM-5.3, one prefill group (4x8 H100, wide EP), request latency with a CPU-tier hit: ~1.9 s without the fix or above the limit, ~0.85 s under it (hits of 2k to 15k tokens).

Correctness: greedy continuation with the tail served from the CPU tier is correct 7/7 (Qwen3 and GLM-5.3).

    pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/   # 644 passed
    pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py         # 41 passed, 1 skipped

## Details

Not a duplicate: no open PR adds sync offload loads (closest: #60574, #58198).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Report every transfer group as loaded in DecodeBenchConnector
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`DecodeBenchConnector` fills a new request's own blocks in every KV cache group, like a P/D transfer, but it inherits the base `get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids`, which reports only the prefix-cacheable groups (what a hash-addressed store holds). A bounded-replay sliding-window group (DeepSeek V4.1) is not prefix-cacheable, so `_load_restores_replay_window` is false and the scheduler replays the last window on the first step of every filled request. That step becomes a prefill of about one window (128 tokens on DeepSeek V4.1) instead of a one-token decode, and with DP every rank leaves the FULL decode graph whenever any rank admits a request, so decode-only benchmarks with this connector do not reflect P/D decode.

This returns `transfer_group_ids`, the same as `NixlConnector` and `MooncakeConnector` since #59197. The connector is synchronous, so `skip_zeroing_group_ids` (async loads only) is unaffected; the only change is that the filled window is taken as is.

## Not a duplicate

No open PR changes the loaded groups of `DecodeBenchConnector`. #61543 skips non-transfer groups on the fill side (a HiSparse crash) and is complementary: with both, the connector fills and reports the same `transfer_group_ids`. #59197 added the replay skip and the NIXL / Mooncake overrides but left this connector on the default.

## Test Plan

- New `test_decode_bench_fill_does_not_replay` in `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py`: the real scheduler with `DecodeBenchConnector` on a full-attention + bounded-replay `SlidingWindowMLASpec` layout; a filled request must start with a one-token step and no replay. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Events] Prevent replay truncation when the send queue fills
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This PR fixes a case where a slow KV-event subscriber can lose replayed batches and the completion marker, leaving it waiting indefinitely.

## Claims

- Set the replay socket's send high-water mark to `buffer_steps + 1`, allowing room for the retained history and its completion marker.
- Add a regression test for a subscriber that waits until the replay burst has finished before reading.

## Validation

- Before the fix, the regression fails with `Replay stalled after 2000 batches`.
- With the fix, all 17 tests in `tests/distributed/test_events.py` pass.

## Details

`ZmqEventPublisher` uses a PUB socket for live events and a separate ROUTER socket for replay. After publishing each batch, it saves the sequence number and payload in an in-memory buffer, which retains up to 10,000 batches by default. Subscribers that detect a sequence gap can request those batches, and the publisher sends them in one burst, followed by a completion marker.

The replay socket keeps ZMQ's default send limit of 1,000 queued messages per client. If a subscriber cannot read quickly enough and that queue fills, the ROUTER silently drops further messages, potentially including the marker. Clients can wait for replay to finish before processing more live events, so losing the marker can freeze its KV routing index.

We set the replay send limit to `buffer_steps + 1` (which matches the buffer size, i.e. the upper limit of how many messages are cached in the replay buffer) before binding the socket. This lets one full replay and its marker fit without requiring the subscriber to read concurrently. Queue memory remains bounded, although the larger limit allows more memory per client.

## Duplicates
**No** open PR fixing this replay queue limit was found. Related PRs [#62391](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62391) and [#53883](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53883) address shutdown cleanup and the Python input queue, respectively.

## AI assistance disclaimer
OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, tests, and this description. I reviewed every line of code in this PR.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Use AITER FlyDSL INT4 QuickReduce when INT4 QuickReduce is selected
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Whenever INT4 QuickReduce is selected (`VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4`) on gfx942/gfx950 with AITER enabled, vLLM creates AITER's FlyDSL INT4 QuickReduce communicator (`aiter.ops.flydsl.QuickAllReduceInt4`, [ROCm/aiter#4970](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4970), merged; TP 2/4/8) next to the HIP one. A bf16, contiguous, 16-byte-aligned payload that HIP QuickReduce would take at the INT4 level runs FlyDSL instead; every other payload runs HIP QuickReduce as before. FlyDSL has no fused RMSNorm kernel yet, so with the fused all-reduce + RMSNorm pass on, such a payload takes FlyDSL all-reduce plus a separate RMSNorm, and the pass is a no-op for it. vLLM warns once when `fuse_allreduce_rms` is on. There is no new environment variable, and QuickReduce itself stays off unless a codec is selected. AITER measures the kernel 29–47% faster than HIP INT4 at TP8 (512 × 4096: 18.1 vs 26.5 µs; 32768 × 5120: 558 vs 1061 µs).

Not a duplicate: searched open and closed PRs for "FlyDSL QuickReduce". [#61021](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61021) and [#61020](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61020) add RMSNorm and MXFP4 epilogues to this kernel and build on it.

## Claims

- bf16 payloads inside the HIP QuickReduce window run 1.2–1.5× faster than the HIP kernel on the same payload (TP4, real kernels). With the fused all-reduce + RMSNorm pass on, FlyDSL all-reduce plus a separate RMSNorm is no slower than the fused-pass route the nightly takes for the same payload, 1.05–2.96× faster at TP2, TP4 and TP8 (table below). fp16 and other payloads run HIP QuickReduce at HIP speed.
- On Qwen3.8-2.4T, TP8, MI355X, serving throughput with this PR is 1.044× stock (geomean of nine cells, ahead in 16 of 18 seed pairs; +4–6% in most prefill-heavy cells, +2% at 1024 / 1024 c256, flat at c128), and median TPOT is 4–6% lower in six of the nine cells. GSM8K is unchanged (0.9726 stock, 0.9726 and 0.9749 with the PR).

## Validation

**Unit tests.** On the PR head `715157803`, stock `nightly-3f1bcfd8` with the PR applied, 4 MI355X visible: `python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_quick_all_reduce.py tests/distributed/test_aiter_rms_fallback.py`: 45 passed, 1 skipped (`test_custom_quick_allreduce_variable_input[8]` needs 8 GPUs), 2 failed. The two failures are `test_custom_quick_allreduce[graph_quickreduce, TP2 x PP2, INT4]` and `[INT3]` (max abs difference 5.0 against 2.5 allowed, and 10.0 against 5.5). They fail identically on `nightly-3f1bcfd8` without this PR. On that stock nightly the three tests below also fail, as they should, since they test this PR's routing. The test makes the second pipeline group all-reduce twice in the graph, and the differences are twice the tolerance, which fits doubled quantization error.
- `test_flydsl_int4_dispatch_falls_back_to_hip` fails if fp16, non-contiguous, misaligned or FP-codec payloads reach FlyDSL.
- `test_close_closes_flydsl_int4` fails if `close` leaves the FlyDSL communicator open.
- `test_rocm_aiter_fused_rmsnorm_skips_fused_kernels_for_flydsl_payloads` fails if a payload FlyDSL owns reaches the fused HIP QR+RMSNorm or custom-AR RMSNorm kernels.

**Kernel routing, TP4, MI355X** (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, INT4, flag on). The last column runs the HIP kernel directly on the same payload. Relative error is against an NCCL all-reduce.

| dtype | Payload | Backend | Rel. error | µs (routed) | µs (HIP kernel) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 | 2 MiB | FlyDSL | 0.110 | 24.0 | 30.4 |
| bf16 | 64 MiB | FlyDSL | 0.110 | 206.5 | 266.0 |
| bf16 | 256 MiB | FlyDSL | 0.110 | 767.8 | 938.9 |
| fp16 | 2 MiB | HIP | 0.121 | 29.4 | 29.1 |
| fp16 | 256 MiB | HIP | 0.121 | 934.5 | 932.7 |

**Kernel routing under the fused all-reduce + RMSNorm pass, MI355X** (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, INT4, `fuse_allreduce_rms` on, hidden 8192, bf16, torch profiler over CUDA-graph replays, device kernel time per all-reduce + RMSNorm). "Nightly" is what `nightly-3f1bcfd8` runs for the payload; "this PR" is FlyDSL all-reduce plus a separate RMSNorm. The runs used the earlier head `2d7514110a`, which routed payloads of at least 2 MiB to FlyDSL; that is the whole HIP QuickReduce window at TP4 and TP8. Payloads below the window run the same custom-AR kernels in both builds. Kernels did not change in `715157803`; at TP2 it also routes 1–2 MiB payloads, which this sweep did not re-run: FlyDSL all-reduce measured 15.8 µs plus a 3.4 µs RMSNorm there, against 23.0 µs for the HIP kernel alone.

| TP | Payload | Tokens | µs nightly | µs this PR | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 2 MiB | 128 | 46.8 | 25.0 | 1.87× |
| 2 | 8 MiB | 512 | 164.6 | 61.4 | 2.68× |
| 2 | 32 MiB | 2048 | 639.7 | 228.2 | 2.80× |
| 2 | 128 MiB | 8192 | 886.9 | 846.4 | 1.05× |
| 4 | 2 MiB | 128 | 29.6 | 21.7 | 1.36× |
| 4 | 8 MiB | 512 | 92.0 | 44.4 | 2.07× |
| 4 | 32 MiB | 2048 | 339.1 | 133.9 | 2.53× |
| 4 | 128 MiB | 8192 | 594.9 | 493.2 | 1.21× |
| 8 | 2 MiB | 128 | 22.0 | 20.3 | 1.09× |
| 8 | 8 MiB | 512 | 56.2 | 36.9 | 1.52× |
| 8 | 32 MiB | 2048 | 190.9 | 103.2 | 1.85× |
| 8 | 128 MiB | 8192 | 502.8 | 322.3 | 1.56× |

**Serving.** `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8, MI355X, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4`, one server per arm from empty vLLM and AITER caches. Arm a is stock `nightly-3f1bcfd8` with `fuse_allreduce_rms` on. Arms b and c are the same nightly with this PR applied (`715157803`), with `fuse_allreduce_rms` off and on. Each cell ran twice with different seeds; the same seeds ran in every arm, and every arm generated identical token counts with no failed requests. Total token throughput, mean of the two seeds:

| ISL / OSL, concurrency | a stock, tok/s | b PR, fusion off | c PR, fusion on | c / a (seed 1, seed 2) | median TPOT a → c, ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2048 / 128, c16 | 7,391 | 7,373 | 7,483 | 1.012 (1.011, 1.014) | 33.1 → 33.2 |
| 2048 / 128, c64 | 12,589 | 13,200 | 13,101 | 1.041 (1.036, 1.045) | 79.4 → 75.8 |
| 8192 / 128, c4 | 9,922 | 10,061 | 10,304 | 1.039 (1.038, 1.039) | 22.5 → 21.5 |
| 8192 / 128, c16 | 16,182 | 17,008 | 17,120 | 1.058 (1.062, 1.054) | 54.7 → 51.4 |
| 32768 / 128, c4 | 15,022 | 16,653 | 16,777 | 1.117 (1.072, 1.167) | 48.4 → 46.1 |
| 60000 / 128, c4 | 16,659 | 17,642 | 17,698 | 1.062 (1.065, 1.059) | 78.0 → 73.0 |
| 128000 / 128, c2 | 13,966 | 14,928 | 14,667 | 1.050 (1.053, 1.047) | 69.8 → 66.0 |
| 1024 / 1024, c128 | 4,478 | 4,490 | 4,471 | 0.999 (1.000, 0.997) | 54.8 → 54.8 |
| 1024 / 1024, c256 | 6,550 | 6,742 | 6,699 | 1.023 (1.024, 1.022) | 74.7 → 73.1 |

Geomean of the nine cell ratios, throughput: c / a 1.044, b / a 1.042; median TPOT c / a 0.963. In 16 of 18 paired c / a throughput ratios the PR is ahead; the other two are the `1024 / 1024, c128` decode cell, where all three arms are within 0.3%. The `2048 / 128, c16` cell is inconclusive (b / a 0.97 and 1.02 across the two seeds). The `32768 / 128, c4` ratios differ between seeds (1.07 and 1.17), so only the direction is supported there. Arms b and c, the two runs of the candidate, agree within 3% in every cell and 0.3% on the geomean. Arm a ran first and was not repeated, so the c / a ratios have no separate A/A control; run-to-run noise at the cell level is the spread between b and c plus the seed-to-seed spread above.

**Accuracy.** GSM8K, 5-shot, `temperature` 0, thinking off, 1319 requested and 1314 scored in every arm: a 0.9726, b 0.9749, c 0.9726 (a binomial standard error is about 0.4%, so these agree).

## Details

- **Routing.** HIP QuickReduce is always initialized and its size window applies first (at least 2 MiB at TP4 and TP8, at least 1 MiB at TP2; 128 tokens at hidden 8192 is 2 MiB). FlyDSL runs a payload that is bf16, contiguous, 16-byte-aligned and at the INT4 level for its size (below `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION_MIN_SIZE_KB` the FP codec runs). There is no FlyDSL size floor of its own: below the HIP window it measured 14% slower than the custom-AR kernel at 0.5 MiB on TP8, so the window must not be widened. A decode batch of 128 tokens or more at hidden 8192 is inside the window and runs FlyDSL; smaller decode payloads stay on the custom-AR kernels, which this PR does not change.
- **Fused all-reduce + RMSNorm.** A payload FlyDSL owns skips the fused HIP QR+RMSNorm and the fused custom-AR RMSNorm kernels and runs all-reduce plus a separate RMSNorm, so `fuse_allreduce_rms` does nothing for it, and vLLM warns once when the pass is on. This is not slower in the measured window: the FlyDSL all-reduce is faster than the HIP kernel on every payload at TP4 and TP8 and within 0.3% at TP2 (32 MiB), and FlyDSL plus a separate RMSNorm is at worst 1.07× slower than the HIP kernel with the fused RMSNorm applied by hand (TP2 at 32 MiB; at TP4 and TP8 it ties or wins), a route the nightly does not take (next bullet). Fusing RMSNorm into the FlyDSL kernel is [#61021](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61021) and the MXFP4 epilogue is [#61020](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61020); both are prefill fusions and need [ROCm/aiter#6369](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6369).
- **The fused HIP QR+RMSNorm did not fire in the image checked.** In `nightly-3f1bcfd8` (AITER 0.1.25) and `nightly-5555a2d8` (AITER 0.1.24.post1), `_get_or_create_aiter_qr_rmsnorm_comm` fails on `aiter.qr_get_handle(ptr)`: AITER's signature is `qr_get_handle(fa, out_ptr)` since [ROCm/aiter#4421](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4421), the call raises `TypeError`, and the bare `except Exception` returns `None`. In both images the function returned `None` for vLLM's own communicator (TP2 on `5555a2d8`, TP2, TP4 and TP8 on `3f1bcfd8`). Fused all-reduces there ran the custom-AR kernel instead. The control image of the earlier A/B (`nightly-92044241`) was not re-checked. This PR does not touch that function.
- **Architecture gate.** The communicator is created when `get_cdna_version() in (3, 4)`: AITER's `QuickAllReduceInt4` supports gfx942 and gfx950 only. It runs AITER kernels, so `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` is the switch that turns it off.
- **Limitations and CI gaps.** The serving A/B has one run of the stock arm and no A/A control. The measured uplift comes from payloads of 2 MiB and up, which only the prefill cells and decode batches of 128 tokens or more reach; at hidden 8192 the kernel sweep predicts the size: FlyDSL saves about 180 µs per all-reduce on a 128 MiB payload at TP8, about 6% of an 8192-token prefill pass over 184 all-reduces, and the 8k / 128 c16 cell measured +6%. The multi-GPU QuickReduce tests skip in CI without GPUs.

commits.pr_title: [Core][Spec Decode] Lookahead block hashes for EAGLE prefix caching
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Part 1 of 2 split from vllm-project/vllm#50897 (implements vllm-project/vllm#50438): **lookahead block hashes** for the local prefix cache. EAGLE, EAGLE3 and MTP drafters write the draft KV at a block's last position from the token after the block, so `main` drops the last matched block on every hit. This PR puts that token into the block hash and removes the drop when no KV connector is configured. KV connector support is in the stacked PR (part 2).

## Claims

- Local prefix-cache hits with EAGLE, EAGLE3 and MTP reach `floor((N - 1) / B) * B`, the same as without speculative decoding, instead of one cache unit less (544–1600 tokens on hybrid attention + Mamba/GDN models). Multi-module MTP with k modules reaches `floor((N - k) / B) * B`.
- A block is reused only when its lookahead token matches, so a hit reads the same draft KV as a cold run.
- New `SpeculativeConfig.disable_lookahead_block_hashes` restores `main`'s behavior. With any KV connector configured, this PR keeps the legacy hashes.
- KV events publish the lookahead token in a new `BlockStored.lookahead_token_ids` field, so consumers can reproduce the hashes.
- Model runners are unchanged; no new CPU/GPU synchronization.

## Validation

Unit tests on this branch (one GB200 node):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/core tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py \
  tests/distributed/test_kv_cache_events.py \
  --ignore tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py -k "not ray"
```

Result: 1,256 passed. `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` is excluded because it launches the `vllm` CLI (see the TODO below).

Hash format CPU cost: one `request_block_hasher` call over a whole prompt, SHA-256, one pinned GB200 Grace core, median of 15 alternating-order rounds of 5 calls. Token IDs are random, and the prompt length is aligned + 1 so every format emits the same hashes; MM rows add a 512-token image every 1,024 tokens. Each variant is the real hasher with only its lookahead branch replaced; an unmodified copy run the same way stays within 0.2% of the real one. Percentages are versus `main`.

- nested: `H((parent, tokens[s:e], (E(s, e), tokens[e], E(e, e + 1))))`, the previous revision of this PR
- expanded window: `H((parent, tokens[s:e + 1], E(s, e + 1)))`
- this PR: `H((parent, tokens[s:e], (E(s, e + 1), tokens[e])))`

| Input | Prompt tokens | B | main | nested | expanded window | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| text | 32K+1 | 16 | 3.166 ms | 4.107 ms (+29.7%) | 3.394 ms (+7.2%) | 3.566 ms (+12.6%) |
| text | 32K+1 | 128 | 0.917 ms | 1.033 ms (+12.6%) | 0.940 ms (+2.5%) | 0.963 ms (+5.0%) |
| text | 32K+1 | 1024 | 0.636 ms | 0.647 ms (+1.7%) | 0.635 ms (-0.2%) | 0.639 ms (+0.5%) |
| text | 128K+1 | 16 | 13.007 ms | 16.770 ms (+28.9%) | 13.945 ms (+7.2%) | 14.406 ms (+10.8%) |
| text | 128K+1 | 128 | 3.805 ms | 4.248 ms (+11.6%) | 3.907 ms (+2.7%) | 3.967 ms (+4.3%) |
| text | 128K+1 | 1024 | 2.705 ms | 2.786 ms (+3.0%) | 2.717 ms (+0.4%) | 2.746 ms (+1.5%) |
| MM | 32K+1 | 16 | 3.777 ms | 5.126 ms (+35.7%) | 4.104 ms (+8.7%) | 4.271 ms (+13.1%) |
| MM | 32K+1 | 128 | 1.013 ms | 1.194 ms (+17.9%) | 1.065 ms (+5.1%) | 1.087 ms (+7.3%) |
| MM | 32K+1 | 1024 | 0.654 ms | 0.675 ms (+3.2%) | 0.658 ms (+0.6%) | 0.660 ms (+0.9%) |

One `E` call instead of two saves 7–17% at B ≤ 128 versus the nested form. The expanded window is cheapest, but its hash input equals a legacy hash with block size `B + 1`; keeping `tokens[e]` in the extra keys costs 3–5% more than it at B = 16 and at most 2.5% at B ≥ 128. With one lookahead token the hasher indexes `tokens[e]` instead of slicing, which builds the same tuple; the slice cost about 7 more points at B = 16.

End-to-end and draft-KV results from the combined PR (vllm-project/vllm#50897, earlier revision; not yet re-run on this split):

| Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B, MTP k=4, 1x GB200, `prefix_repetition` | `main` | lookahead hashes |
|---|---|---|
| Prefix-cache hit rate | 72.7% | **85.0%** |
| Request throughput | 9.09 req/s | **12.43 req/s** |
| Mean / median TTFT | 404 / 304 ms | **318 / 226 ms** |
| GSM8K 5-shot | 0.4359 | 0.4359 |

Hit length, Qwen3.5-2B + MTP k=1, unit 544, 1,367-token prompt sent twice: `main` without spec decode 1088, `main` with MTP 544, lookahead hashes 1088.

Draft-KV check (KV of the hit blocks vs a cold run, bf16 max abs diff): Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3 0.09–0.14 (negative control with a stale lookahead token: 7.55); Qwen3.5-2B MTP 0.19 (control: 14.53).

TODO before review: re-run `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py`, `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` and the benchmark on GPU.

## Details

**Enablement.** `get_num_hash_lookahead_tokens` (`v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`) returns `L = num_prefill_lookahead_tokens` (1, or k for multi-module MTP with k modules) when `use_eagle_block_drop()`, `not disable_lookahead_block_hashes`, prefix caching is on and there is no KV transfer config; otherwise 0, which keeps the legacy hashes and the block drop. DFlash and DSpark build draft KV from target hidden states alone; vllm-project/vllm#54163 removes them from `use_eagle_block_drop()`, after which they keep the legacy hashes with no drop. Until then they get lookahead hashes too, which is correct but unnecessary. `num_hash_lookahead_tokens` replaces the former boolean flag through the KV cache manager, coordinator, block pool and scheduler. Part 2 replaces the last condition with a per-connector capability.

**Hashing.** `get_request_block_hasher(..., num_hash_lookahead_tokens=L)` hashes a block `[s, e)` only once tokens up to `e + L - 1` are in `all_token_ids`, as `H((parent, tokens[s:e], (E(s, e + L), *tokens[e:e + L])))`; for `L = 1` that is `(E(s, e + 1), tokens[e])`. `E` is `generate_block_hash_extra_keys` over the block and its lookahead tokens, called once per block, so MM inputs or prompt embeddings there are covered too; the MM cursor then steps back to the first input the next block overlaps. The hashed tokens stay the block's tokens, and the `(E, token)` shape keeps these hashes apart from legacy ones; hashing `tokens[s:e + L]` instead would equal a legacy hash with block size `B + L`. Different `L` give different tuple lengths. All KV cache groups share these hashes.

**KV events.** `BlockStored.lookahead_token_ids` holds `tokens[e:e + L]` per block, and `extra_keys` keeps its untagged per-block shape but covers `[s, e + L)`. A block hash is reproducible from `token_ids`, `extra_keys` and `lookahead_token_ids` (`test_kv_events_reconstruct_lookahead_block_hashes`). Consumers that ignore the new field still decode events, but blocks with the same tokens at the same position can now carry different hashes, so routers that index one hash per position need to key on the lookahead tokens. The extra field widens the msgpack map header of every `BlockStored` (fixmap to map16); decoded contents are unchanged. `examples/features/kv_events/kv_events_subscriber.py` includes the field.

**Caching.** Blocks are cached at allocation, as without lookahead hashes; `SingleTypeKVCacheManager.cache_blocks` stops at the last hashed block. At request finish, `update_from_output` caches the block whose lookahead the last sampled token completes.

**Drop removal.** The scheduler clears `use_eagle_block_drop`. `KVCacheCoordinator.drop_eagle_group_ids` is empty in this mode and drives the per-group drop and `replay_boundaries`, so the last-block drop, the Mamba checkpoint back-off and the replay-boundary shift are all skipped from one place. `eagle_group_ids` stays, since `mamba_shared_prefix_checkpoint` still applies.

**Docs.** A new "Prefix caching" section in `docs/features/speculative_decoding/README.md` covers the default, `disable_lookahead_block_hashes` and `BlockStored.lookahead_token_ids`.

**Why it is correct.** The drafter writes the draft KV at `e - 1` (input `(h_{e-1}, token e)`) in the step that prefills or samples token `e`. The hash exists only once token `e` is in `all_token_ids`, which never holds draft or in-flight tokens, so a cached block's draft KV is written by the end of that step. With k-module MTP, module j writes its KV at `p` from token `p + j`, so the hash waits for tokens up to `e + k - 1`. `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator` re-prefills a slot written from a rejected draft in the step that samples its replacement, and the coordinator already keeps the last `k - 1` computed tokens out of the cache.

**Limitations**

- Multi-module MTP lookahead hashes are covered by unit tests only; the draft-KV check against a cold run has not been run for them yet.
- HiSparse requires `HiSparseConnector`, so like other connectors it keeps the legacy hashes and the block drop. Its host tier publishes pages once their host copies finish; whether those copies include the last position's draft KV needs GPU validation before part 2 lets `HiSparseConnector` opt in.
- Streaming-input sessions are not supported. When a turn ends on a lookahead boundary, the block cached with the discarded sampled token keeps that hash (its draft KV was written from that token), so later blocks of the session are unreachable by prefix lookups from other requests.
- Hybrid models lose the hit when a prompt diverges exactly at the producer's last retained Mamba boundary (0 vs one unit on `main`); see vllm-project/vllm#50897 for the reproducer.

<details><summary>Duplicate-work check</summary>

Split from vllm-project/vllm#50897 by the same author. No other open PR adds the successor token to the prefix-cache key (vllm-project/vllm#44986, vllm-project/vllm#45614, vllm-project/vllm#48375 and vllm-project/vllm#39171 change when the drop applies, not the key).

</details>

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Read GPU Engram tables from peers' HBM instead of DP collectives
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With `cpu_offload: false`, DeepSeek-V4.1's Engram tables live in HBM, but every lookup still goes through DP collectives: a pynccl `all_gather` of the hash ids and an `all_to_all_single` of the rows on the node-local `edp` group. Decode runs in FULL CUDA graphs, which do not honor `eager_break_during_capture`, so these collectives are captured next to MegaMoE's cross-rank kernels. In DEP decode on GB200, every rank then blocks in `graph.replay()` of the same decode graph at the first real step (seen with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`); host-offloaded tables, with no NCCL in the graph, never hang. I did not pin down the exact NCCL/MegaMoE interaction. This PR removes the collectives instead: GPU tables are row-sharded over the Engram DP group in symmetric memory, and each rank looks up only its own tokens, reading every row from the owning peer's HBM. Lookups need no collective, barrier or graph break.

* **Kernel.** `_engram_lookup_kernel` gains `PEER_ROWS`. With it, `weight` is a per-rank pointer table: a row's owner is `id // PEER_ROWS`, and its scales follow the rows in the same symmetric buffer. Tables are read-only after loading, so reads need no synchronization.
* **When.** `cpu_offload: false`, TP=1 and an Engram DP group (co-located DP replicas). The table sets `dp_size = 1`, as `dp_shared_memory` does, and `DeepseekV4Model` reads that to skip the hash gather and dummy hashes. Host tables keep `dp_shared_memory` / `EngramPeerExchange`, since symmetric memory cannot map another process's host memory.
* **Across nodes.** By default the group stays node-local. With `embedding_across_dp: true` (off by default), GPU tables are split over every DP rank, e.g. 1/32 of the table per GPU at DEP32; all DP ranks must then share one NVLink domain, as on GB200 NVL72. A group with the DP group's ranks reuses `_DP` instead of building a second communicator: a separate 32-rank group cost ~1.1 GiB/GPU and failed `gpu_memory_utilization=0.95`.
* **Not covered.** GPU tables with TP > 1 keep head sharding and its collectives. Peer mode stages BF16 rows per layer rather than `EngramBatch`'s packed MXFP8 rows, so `wkv` quantizes its own input; feeding packed peer rows to `EngramBatch` is a possible follow-up.

## Where it matters

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode-only on GB200, DEP16 / DEP32 (DP x TP1 + EP), 16 requests/rank, MegaMoE, MegaAttention, DSpark (5 tokens, synthetic acceptance 3.51), EPLB, full decode CUDA graphs, `DecodeBenchConnector` replaying an agentic coding trace. Unprofiled steady state (+60 to +240 s), one run each, on a development tree based on `fe4df3df` with #61767; its Engram code is identical to main. Without this PR, `cpu_offload: false` hangs in this setup, so the baseline is the default host offload. GPU tables use `embedding_across_dp: true`.

| | host offload | GPU tables, peer read |
| -- | --: | --: |
| DEP16 step (ms) | 14.13 | 13.71 |
| DEP16 output (tok/s/GPU) | 3,777 | 3,827 |
| DEP32 step (ms) | 13.15 | 12.90 |
| DEP32 output (tok/s/GPU) | 3,877 | 3,939 |
| Model memory, DEP16 / DEP32 (GiB/GPU) | | 28.9 / 20.3 |

## Microbenchmark

Both Engram layers' lookups for one decode step, 96 tokens/rank, 16 ranks on 4 GB200 nodes, CUDA graph replay with fresh ids, median over ranks.

| Table layout | us/step |
| -- | --: |
| Host UVA (offload) | 233-324 |
| HBM, heads over 4 GPUs + `all_gather` + `all_to_all` (main; hangs in FULL graphs) | 46.7 |
| HBM, rows over 16 GPUs + `all_gather` + `reduce_scatter` | 180.6 |
| HBM, rows over 16 GPUs, peer read (this PR) | 19.8 |

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/parallel_state.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py
```

* `test_engram_table_shared_across_dp_replicas` (4 GPUs): the TP1 x DP4 GPU-table case now takes the peer path, asserts that no DP `all_gather` runs, and replays a FULL CUDA graph with fresh ids.
* `test_engram_group_creation_honors_model_and_options`: TP1 x DP4 cases for the node-local group vs `embedding_across_dp`, and `_DP` reuse.

## Test Result

On 4 x GB200: 29 passed. Pre-commit (ruff, format, typos, mypy) passes.

## Accuracy

GSM8K with lm-eval 0.4.13: 1319 problems, 5-shot completions, temperature 0, 1024-token cap, concurrency 32. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MegaAttention, MXFP4 indexer cache with sparse logits, DeepGEMM mega MoE, DSpark (5 tokens), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 8192`.

| | Engram tables | strict match | flexible extract |
| -- | -- | --: | --: |
| this PR, DEP8 over two GB200 nodes | GPU, rows over all 8 DP ranks (peer read) | 92.57% (±0.72) | 92.72% |
| #61371, DEP4 | host offload | 92.87% (±0.71) | |

The first revision of this PR gave 92.87% / 92.95% on the same setup.

To successfully run kimi, we also rely on a MLA fix(https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63530)

commits.pr_title: [ROCm] Octave KV (`ROCM_OCTAVE`): native 3-bit KV cache backend for AMD GPUs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Adds `ROCM_OCTAVE`, an attention backend that keeps the KV cache of full-attention layers at 3-4 bits per value, with native HIP kernels for RDNA3 (gfx1100) and MI300X (gfx942). Select it with `--kv-cache-dtype octave_k3v3`, `octave_k3v4` or `octave_k3v3_compact` (216, 248 and 196 bytes per slot at head size 256, against 1024 for fp16). RFC: #59773. `docs/design/rocm_octave.md` describes the format and the per-architecture contract. ## Claims - **Capacity:** - On 4× RX 7900 XTX with Qwen3.8-27B, 4.6× the KV tokens of fp16. - On one MI300X, 1.95× the tokens of AITER's fp8 cache (7.0M vs 3.6M, i.e. 53 vs 27 concurrent 128k requests). - **Quality:** GSM8K and a 126k needle-in-a-haystack test match fp16 and fp8 on both architectures. Next-token NLL at 380k is +0.0009 to +0.0015 nats over fp16. - **Speed:** - On MI300X, decode for one request matches AITER fp8. Per layer it is faster from 32k on (65 vs 103 µs at 128k). - On RDNA3 at 380k, per layer, decode is 4.6× faster than TurboQuant and MTP verification 11× faster. - **Works with MTP and CUDA graphs.** No host syncs in the metadata builder. We have served it in production on RDNA3 since October 2, 2026. - **Guarded to the validated architectures**, gfx1100 and gfx942: - CMake builds the sources and registers the ops only for them. - `supports_compute_capability` rejects other devices. - The tests skip elsewhere. ## Validation **Models.** Qwen3.8-27B W4A16 (compressed-tensors, int4, group 32). To reproduce, [`cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4`](https://huggingface.co/cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4) is a public checkpoint with the same scheme and architecture; KV token counts will differ slightly. **Tests** (`pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_octave.py`), on this branch at 28aa54ed9a (merged with `main` 3897f95cf1): | | gfx1100 | gfx942 | |---|---|---| | `test_rocm_octave.py` | 105 passed | 87 passed, 18 skipped (sparse decode is gfx1100-only) | | Octave kernels with scratch in the built `.so` | 0 of 108 | 0 of 108 | - The tests compare store, decode and prefill with the PyTorch reference for all three cache dtypes. That covers: - the native and the portable decode; - 1 and 4 query tokens (MTP); - padded queries and 1-256 KV splits; - fp16 and bf16; - prefill over a cached prefix with several requests; - the sparse (QSA) decode. - To check that the tests can fail, I broke the kernels on purpose several times: a wrong codebook, a least-squares scale, a wrong `log2(e)`, a missing query debias. Each time the relevant tests failed. - `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` on gfx942: served `cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4` with `octave_k3v3` and MTP k=3 through 40 GSM8K questions with no sync error (97.5%). - pre-commit passes on the changed files, except `update-dockerfile-graph`, which needs `/bin/bash` and cannot run on my machine. mypy (CI stage) passes. - CI: the AMD `kernels/attention` step runs `test_rocm_octave.py` on its MI300 runners (gfx942). gfx1100 is not in CI; it was validated locally as above. **MI300X end to end.** Setup: - 1× MI300X, TP1, fp16, MTP k=3, `--max-model-len 131072`; only the cache dtype changes between rows. - GSM8K: `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, chat, thinking off, 200 questions, temperature 0.6. - NIAH: details below. - Speed: `vllm bench serve`. - The fp8 row is forced with `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA`. With only `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, vLLM picks `ROCM_ATTN`. | KV cache | KV tokens | GSM8K | NIAH | decode at 126k | TPOT 1 user, 8k / 32k / 100k | TTFT 100k | 16 users, 8k | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | `octave_k3v3` | 7,014,973 | 98.0 | 28/28 | 52 tok/s | 15 / 18 / 16 ms | 20.2 s | 221 tok/s | | `octave_k3v4` | 6,391,547 | 97.5 | 28/28 | 52 tok/s | 15 / 15 / 19 ms | 20.2 s | 226 tok/s | | `octave_k3v3_compact` | 7,446,005 | 97.0 | 28/28 | 50 tok/s | 16 / 18 / 16 ms | 20.1 s | 211 tok/s | | fp8, `ROCM_AITER_FA` | 3,597,048 | 97.0 | 28/28 | 50 tok/s | 15 / 17 / 16 ms | 18.6 s | 235 tok/s | | fp16, `ROCM_ATTN` | 1,952,899 | 97.0 | 28/28 | 6 tok/s | 22 / 45 / 108 ms | 23.1 s | 120 tok/s | AITER is ahead with 16 users and in time to first token at 100k, which points at our prefill over a cached prefix; that is the next thing to work on.
MI300X: NIAH in detail The haystack is vLLM's own Python source, cut to 126k tokens. 16 keys are inserted every ~7.7k tokens, each a line such as `# PROJECT KEY Aldebaran: WK3DEGZD`, with star names as look-alike labels and random 8-character values. The same document is cut at 32k, 64k and 126k, which hold 4, 8 and 16 keys. For each key present the model is asked, thinking off, for only that key's value; an answer counts if it contains the exact value. Keys sit between 3% and 95% of the context. | KV cache | 32k (4 keys) | 64k (8 keys) | 126k (16 keys) | another key's value returned | |---|---|---|---|---| | `octave_k3v3` | 4/4 | 8/8 | 16/16 | 0 | | `octave_k3v4` | 4/4 | 8/8 | 16/16 | 0 | | `octave_k3v3_compact` | 4/4 | 8/8 | 16/16 | 0 | | fp8, `ROCM_AITER_FA` | 4/4 | 8/8 | 16/16 | 0 | | fp16, `ROCM_ATTN` | 4/4 | 8/8 | 16/16 | 0 | The model saturates this task at 128k. So it shows that the 3-bit cache loses no retrieval there; it does not rank the formats. The harder test is the 800k key curve in the RFC, where the keys start to blur only past 640k, because of the model and not the cache.

No request failed. Each cell is median TTFT / median TPOT / output tok/s. Random tokens give MTP a low acceptance, the same for every row. | KV cache | 8k, 1 user | 32k, 1 user | 100k, 1 user | 8k, 16 users | |---|---|---|---|---| | `octave_k3v3` | 1.55 s / 15.3 ms / 51.3 | 5.99 s / 18.1 ms / 33.4 | 20.2 s / 15.6 ms / 17.9 | 3.34 s / 62.1 ms / 221 | | `octave_k3v4` | 1.55 s / 15.4 ms / 52.4 | 6.06 s / 15.3 ms / 35.8 | 20.2 s / 19.2 ms / 17.1 | 3.95 s / 57.0 ms / 226 | | `octave_k3v3_compact` | 1.57 s / 16.2 ms / 50.2 | 6.73 s / 17.6 ms / 32.4 | 20.1 s / 15.6 ms / 17.9 | 3.27 s / 57.2 ms / 211 | | fp8, `ROCM_AITER_FA` | 1.57 s / 15.2 ms / 49.3 | 5.53 s / 17.1 ms / 34.1 | 18.6 s / 16.2 ms / 19.0 | 3.29 s / 49.9 ms / 235 | | fp16, `ROCM_ATTN` | 1.64 s / 22.5 ms / 36.8 | 5.78 s / 44.6 ms / 16.9 | 23.1 s / 108.4 ms / 6.2 | 7.26 s / 112.4 ms / 120 | Without MTP, to compare with UltraQuant (#57057), which needs bf16 here: | KV cache | KV tokens | 8k, 1 user | 32k, 1 user | 100k, 1 user | 8k, 16 users | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `octave_k3v3` (fp16) | 9,437,184 | 1.57 s / 51.9 ms / 18.2 | 5.28 s / 52.2 ms / 16.0 | 19.1 s / 52.6 ms / 11.1 | 10.9 s / 82.0 ms / 157 | | `ultraquant_4bit` (bf16) | 7,730,626 | 1.84 s / 58.5 ms / 16.1 | 6.24 s / 66.0 ms / 12.8 | 20.3 s / 87.5 ms / 7.9 | 14.0 s / 94.5 ms / 135 | On gfx942 UltraQuant's FlyDSL decode is not used, because it targets gfx950 and does not cover 6 query heads per KV head, so this is its Triton fallback. With MTP k=3 its output was not usable on this setup (GSM8K 1%, NIAH 0/28); without MTP it is correct (GSM8K 98.0, NIAH 28/28). This says nothing about UltraQuant on gfx950.
MI300X: attention per layer `benchmarks/attention_benchmarks`, 6 query heads, 1 KV head. | | `octave_k3v3` | fp8, AITER | |---|---|---| | decode, 1 token at 8k | 25 µs | 16 µs | | decode, 1 token at 32k | 32 µs | 33 µs | | decode, 1 token at 128k | 65 µs | 103 µs | | decode, 16 requests at 32k | 227 µs | 323 µs | | decode, 64 requests at 8k | 220 µs | 352 µs | | MTP verify, 4 tokens at 32k | 61 µs | — | Prefill, against `ROCM_AITER_FA` with an fp16 cache: - 8k with no prefix: 2.76 vs 2.50 ms. - Two 2k chunks over an 8k prefix: 3.28 vs 6.76 ms. - A 2k chunk over a 32k prefix: 5.44 vs 7.15 ms.
RDNA3 (4× RX 7900 XTX, TP4) evaluation Setup: - 8 GB of KV cache per GPU, same image and flags for every row. - GSM8K: chat, thinking off, 500 questions, temperature 0.6, no MTP so that TurboQuant is correct. - NLL: one 380k-token document. | KV cache | Bytes | GSM8K | NLL over fp16 | |---|---|---|---| | fp16 | 1024 | 91.8 | — | | `turboquant_k3v4_nc` | 230 | 89.8 | +0.00155 | | `octave_k3v4` | 248 | 91.4 | +0.00086 | | `octave_k3v3` | 216 | 92.4 | +0.00125 | | `octave_k3v3_compact` | 196 | 91.8 | +0.00150 | Attention per layer at 380k (one TP4 shard): | | fp16 | `turboquant_k3v4_nc` | `octave_k3v3_compact` | `octave_k3v3` | |---|---|---|---|---| | decode, 1 token | 2370 µs | 2565 µs | 563 µs | 614 µs | | MTP verify, 4 tokens | 48.8 ms | 6.65 ms | 0.58 ms | 0.62 ms | | prefill, 2048-token chunk | 125.6 ms | 86.6 ms | 60.8 ms | 63.9 ms | Time to first token at 380k, end to end with MTP and a cold prefix: - `octave_k3v3_compact`: 297 s; - fp16: 371 s; - TurboQuant: 621 s. At 100k all three are within 8%, because the GEMMs and the all-reduce dominate. When I replaced the metadata builder the backend first inherited with its own, I checked that nothing moved (TP4, MTP, GSM8K 500 at concurrency 6): - GSM8K: 92.2 → 91.8; - MTP acceptance: 83.33% → 83.39%; - output: 216.1 → 216.8 tok/s.
Sparse attention (qwen4_exp QSA) evaluation Setup: - 4x RX 7900 XTX, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A16 (asymmetric, g32), TP4, fp16, `--max-num-batched-tokens 512`, no prefix caching. - NLL from `prompt_logprobs` over 12 documents of ~8k tokens, split at position 2048, and over 24 short documents. - Values in nats over fp16; mean NLL repeats to about ±0.003 nats. | KV cache | KV tokens | NLL pos >= 2048 | NLL pos < 2048 | NLL short | |---|---|---|---|---| | fp16 | 47,409 | 1.0856 | 1.6707 | 1.1788 | | `octave_k3v3`, no window | 155,930 | +0.0395 | +0.0851 | +0.0708 | | `octave_k3v3` | 155,930 | +0.0163 | -0.0221 | +0.0085 | That run used our fork for the fp16 port of QSA and two RDNA3 MoE fixes, which go in separate PRs. On this branch alone the QSA path is bf16, like upstream.
## Details What changes. Most of the PR is new files: - `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_octave.py`: the format and its PyTorch reference, which defines the byte layout. - `vllm/v1/attention/backends/rocm_octave_attn.py`: the backend and its metadata builder. - `csrc/attention/octave_*`, the kernels: - store, reduce, rotation and a portable decode, shared by both architectures; - WMMA decode and prefill for gfx1100; - MFMA decode and prefill for gfx942; - the op registration in `octave_torch_bindings.cpp`. - Tests, docs, and `--model` plus the new cache dtypes in `benchmarks/attention_benchmarks`. Changes to existing files are small: - the three cache dtypes in `vllm/config/cache.py`, `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` and `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`; - the backend in the registry and in the ROCm platform's selection; - the sources in `CMakeLists.txt`; - `customize_spec` now runs under the current vLLM config, because the backend needs the model's rotary dims to size the slot; - in `qwen4_exp` (QSA), Octave as the main cache through a sparse decode, with the new fused QSA prepare turned off for an Octave cache, since it writes raw BF16 K/V. Nothing changes for other backends or cache dtypes. Design choices a reviewer may want to know about: - **Native kernels only.** There is no Triton fallback; an architecture is added once it has its own kernels and passes the tests and an end-to-end run. The RFC lists what each one needs. - **The metadata builder is the backend's own.** It builds the per-query maps on the device without host syncs, supports `UNIFORM_BATCH` CUDA graphs, and refreshes the maps between fused MTP draft steps. - **On gfx942**: - QK runs on `v_mfma_i32_16x16x32_i8`, with the query split into high and low int8 halves. - V is widened to fp16 by one `v_perm`: each codebook byte becomes an exact fp16 denormal, which the MI300 MFMA keeps. - The decode file is built with `-amdgpu-mfma-vgpr-form`, so the accumulators do not halve the occupancy. - **Supported models.** Head size 256 with 64 RoPE dims, i.e. Qwen3-Next and Qwen3.5 / 3.6 / 3.8. - The decode handles up to 8 query heads per KV head on each GPU. - The sparse decode and the exact sink/recent window are QSA-only and gfx1100-only for now. - Head size 128 is the next step. - **Size.** This is a large PR: about 1.4k lines of gfx942 kernels on top of the RDNA3 ones. Each architecture lives in its own file behind the same `octave_prefill` / `octave_decode` entry points, so it can be reviewed and later removed on its own. **Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs and issues for `octave`, `turboquant rocm`, `kv cache 3-bit`, `kv cache quantization hip` and `lloyd-max kv`. The closest are: - UltraQuant (#57057): FP4 with FlyDSL for gfx950, built on TurboQuant. - KVarN (#46613 / #46812): Triton, CUDA-first. - #43835: HIP int8/int4 for CDNA. - #40396: a Triton TurboQuant decode for MI300X. - #53231: TurboQuant for Gemma 4 on ROCm. - #59132: Triton attention for RDNA without KV quantization. None targets RDNA with native kernels, and none runs below 8 bits with MTP on ROCm. **AI assistance.** I used AI assistance to write this PR: Claude, and Qwen3.8-27B running locally on the boxes it was measured on. I have reviewed every changed line, ran the tests and evaluations above, and can answer for the change. ---

commits.pr_title: [Fast Start] Key the weight cache on MoE and linear kernel backends
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Part of the cache-key audit in the Fast Start roadmap (#56049).

`process_weights_after_loading` converts weights into the selected kernel backend's layout, for example shuffled or repacked. Weights processed for one backend are therefore wrong for another. `WeightCacheKey` did not include the kernel backends, so an `ipc_cache` engine whose `--moe-backend` or `--linear-backend` differed from the daemon's still mapped the daemon's weights.

The NVFP4 MoE pre-processed path has a guard, but it only checks the **engine's** backend. That leaves one case silently wrong:

- the daemon runs with `--moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass`, so the weights are in CUTLASS layout;
- the engine runs with `auto`, which resolves to `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` on B300;
- the engine maps the CUTLASS-layout weights, `/health` returns 200, and every completion is garbage.

This PR adds `moe_backend`, `linear_backend` and `linear_backend_per_quant` to `WeightCacheKey`. The daemon and the IPC loader both build the key from `vllm_config.kernel_config`. A backend mismatch is now reported as a key mismatch on the backend field before any tensor is mapped. With `fallback=true` (the default) the engine then loads from disk.

The key uses the **configured** backends rather than the resolved ones. This is conservative:
- A daemon on `auto` and an engine on the backend `auto` resolves to counts as a miss and falls back to disk.
- Two `auto` configs that resolve differently, e.g. because of different environment variables, are not caught.

Keying on the resolved backend would close both gaps. It needs the resolution to run before the key is built, so I left it for a follow-up.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k "not cold_start"`
  - New `test_ipc_cache_key_tracks_kernel_backends` covers matching and mismatched `moe_backend`, `linear_backend` and `linear_backend_per_quant`, on both the initial load and a standalone `load_weights` reload.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files.
- End to end on B300 with Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4, TP1, `--load-format ipc_cache`, zero_copy mode, `--enforce-eager`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.6`, `--max-model-len 8192`. Each case runs one greedy completion of "The capital of France is", comparing `main` with this PR.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 52 passed.

| Daemon `--moe-backend` | Engine `--moe-backend` | `fallback` | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer_trtllm` | `flashinfer_trtllm` | false | — | Maps 1444 tensors, KV 142.04 GiB, output " Paris. Which of the following is the capital of Germany? …" |
| `flashinfer_trtllm` | `flashinfer_cutlass` | false | `RuntimeError: pre-processed weights require FLASHINFER_TRTLLM backend …` while building the model | `CacheConfigMismatchError: WeightCacheKey mismatch on fields: ['moe_backend']`, raised before mapping |
| `flashinfer_trtllm` | `flashinfer_cutlass` | true | — | "Weight cache unusable (… ['moe_backend']); falling back to disk loading", then serves " Paris. …" |
| `flashinfer_cutlass` | `auto` (resolves to TRTLLM) | false | **Maps 1396 tensors, `/health` 200, output " Ivanka保卫 offence neighbours organisation centre centre defence …"** | `CacheConfigMismatchError: … ['moe_backend']` |

commits.pr_title: [Fast Start] Detect weight cache daemon exit in zero-copy engines
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Part of the **Daemon-loss semantics** item in #56049.

The roadmap assumed that if the weight cache daemon exits, a running zero-copy engine's weights become invalid. **That is not what happens.** On B300 + Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 (TP1, `zero_copy`, `fallback: false`):

| | `main` |
|---|---|
| greedy output before daemon `kill -9` | `" Paris. The capital of Germany is Berlin. The capital of Spain is Madrid. ..."` |
| greedy output after daemon `kill -9` | identical |
| `/health` after daemon loss | 200 |
| GPU 0 memory: engine + daemon → after daemon kill | 167.2 GB → 165.5 GB (only the daemon's context is freed) |
| after starting a replacement daemon | 184.5 GB, and the engine's output is still identical |

The CUDA driver keeps IPC-imported allocations alive until the importing process exits. So failing fast would kill a healthy engine. The actual hazards are silent:

- a restarted daemon holds a **second copy** of the weights on the GPU, and the old copy is pinned until the engine exits;
- the engine never learns that the daemon it mapped from is gone, so nothing tells the operator.

This PR makes the loss observable:

- **Daemon:** a new `watch` command. The daemon keeps the connection open for its lifetime, so it closes exactly when that daemon instance exits, whether it crashes or shuts down. A daemon restarted on the same socket does not mask the loss. Watches of engines that have exited are pruned on the next watch.
- **Engine (`IpcModelLoader`, zero-copy only):** after mapping the weights, a background `WeightCacheDaemonWatch` thread waits on the connection. On EOF it logs a warning that explains the consequences and sets `IpcModelLoader.daemon_lost`.
- **Compatibility:** daemons that predate `watch` reject it and loading proceeds unchanged. A failed watch is best-effort and never triggers the disk fallback.

Not in this PR (left for the rest of the roadmap item): surfacing `daemon_lost` in engine health checks or metrics, and an opt-in policy to exit the engine on daemon loss, so orchestrators can restart both and reclaim the pinned copy.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k "not cold_start"`, including the new tests:
  - `test_ipc_loader_detects_daemon_exit`: two engines watch one daemon, the daemon exits, both detect it; a watcher whose engine exited is pruned.
  - `test_ipc_loader_skips_watch_on_old_daemon`.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` (ruff, mypy, etc.).
- End-to-end on B300, TP1 daemon (`vllm preload`) and `vllm serve ... --load-format ipc_cache --model-loader-extra-config '{"socket_dir": DIR, "mode": "zero_copy", "fallback": false}' --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 --max-model-len 8192`:
  1. greedy completion, then `kill -9` of the daemon rank, then completion and `/health`;
  2. new daemon → engine A → stop A → engine B (warm restart and watcher pruning);
  3. `SIGTERM` of the daemon launcher while engine B is running.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 45 passed. pre-commit: all hooks pass.
- `kill -9` of the daemon: the engine logs `Weight cache daemon at .../vllm_weight_cache_<id>.sock exited. This engine keeps serving: ...` about 0.1 s later. Greedy output is identical before and after, and `/health` returns 200.
- `SIGTERM` of the daemon: also detected.
- Warm restart A → B: both map 1444 tensors. `Available KV cache memory: 140.06 GiB`, the same as `main`. Outputs are identical. The daemon's socket fd count stays at 13 (A's watch was pruned, B's was added). No errors in the daemon log.
- The final change (catching every exception from the watch request instead of only `ConnectionError`/`OSError`) only touches an error path and landed after the e2e run. Unit tests and pre-commit were re-run on it.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Select one structured outputs backend for every route
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

EngineCore compiles every structured-output request with the backend of the first one it sees. The Rust frontend sends gRPC constraints and parser-built output grammars as xgrammar, but every other HTTP constraint as guidance (#44729), so one server that takes both kinds of traffic is order-dependent: after a native constraint reaches the engine first, every later strict, `required`, or named tool call and every `response_format` composed with a reasoning parser fails with `KeyError: 'triggers'` (HTTP 500). This PR makes every Rust route use one backend, chosen by the operator with `--structured-outputs-config.backend` and defaulting to xgrammar, as Python's `auto` does for most requests. It is the follow-up named in #61892.

## Claims

- Every Rust route (chat, completions, gRPC) sends one backend: `--structured-outputs-config.backend`, default `xgrammar`. `auto` selects xgrammar; `guidance`, `outlines`, and `lm-format-enforcer` are accepted. A server no longer depends on which request arrives first.
- With xgrammar, Rust HTTP rejects JSON schemas whose keywords xgrammar ignores with 400, as gRPC does since #61892 and as Python does with `backend=xgrammar`.
- With another backend, chat does not build parser output grammars (they are xgrammar structural tags): the request keeps its own constraint, which the engine applies after reasoning, and tool calls are parsed without a grammar. `--tool-strict-level function|parameter` fails startup unless the backend is xgrammar.
- Constraints the selected backend cannot compile return 400 instead of failing in EngineCore, following Python's per-backend validation: `format`-shape structural tags on guidance, and the constraint kinds outlines and LM Format Enforcer reject.
- `vllm-rs serve` forwards `--structured-outputs-config` to the managed engine, so engine-side options such as `disable_any_whitespace` take effect.

## Validation

GPU smoke on GB200, Qwen3-8B with `--reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser hermes` via `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve`. Same request sequence per server, starting with a native `/v1/completions` constraint; the completions prompts close the think block, since the engine's reasoning gate otherwise waits for `</think>` before applying a raw completions constraint.

| Request (in order) | `main` | This PR, default (xgrammar) | This PR, `backend=guidance` |
|---|---|---|---|
| completions `choice` | 200, valid | 200, valid | 200, valid |
| chat `tool_choice=required` | **500** (`KeyError: 'triggers'`) | 200, `get_weather` call | 200, `get_weather` call |
| chat `response_format` json_schema | **500** | 200, valid JSON | 200, valid JSON |
| chat strict tool, `tool_choice=auto` | **500** | 200, `get_weather` call | 200, `get_weather` call |
| completions `regex` | 200, valid | 200, valid | 200, valid |
| completions json_schema with `multipleOf` | 200, enforced (guidance) | **400** (xgrammar ignores `multipleOf`) | 200, enforced |

Rust tests on the branch tip: `cargo nextest run -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-text -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-managed-engine -p vllm-parser` (1806 passed), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --check`. New tests:

- `chat_structured_outputs_use_configured_backend` (routes): a chat request with a strict tool and `response_format` through a mock engine; the engine request carries the configured backend, a structural tag with xgrammar and the request's own JSON schema with guidance. With the chat-side backend check removed, the guidance case fails (lowering rejects the `format`-shape tag with 400).
- `lower_sampling_params_validates_against_configured_backend`, `backend_rejects_constraint_kinds_it_cannot_compile`, and `engine_structured_outputs_serializes_through_raw_shape` (msgpack round trip).
- CLI: config parsing on `vllm-rs serve` and the `--args-json` bootstrap path, `auto`, forwarding to the managed engine, and the `--tool-strict-level` startup check.

## Details

**Root cause.** `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_init` creates one backend from the first structured request and keeps it until shutdown. Python chooses `_backend` in `SamplingParams` validation, which the Rust frontend skips, so #44729 defaulted Rust to guidance; guidance handled `choice`, which xgrammar could not compile then. Parser-built output grammars (#46057) and gRPC (#61892) later moved to xgrammar, and guidance reads only the legacy `triggers`/`structures` structural tag.

**Where the backend lives.** The backend is now a field of the EngineCore request type only (`EngineCoreStructuredOutputsParams`). `StructuredOutputsParams`, the type the HTTP/gRPC entry points and chat build, carries no backend, so nothing picks one implicitly. `TextRequestProcessor` holds the configured backend, and text lowering, which HTTP and gRPC share, attaches it and validates the final constraint against it. gRPC no longer selects a backend itself.

**Why one backend per server, not per request.** The engine still holds one backend, so a per-request choice would bring the order dependence back. Python's `auto` fallback has the same limit in a mixed workload. Engine-side multi-backend support (#62246, draft) would allow request-level selection later; a single configured backend maps onto a one-element list then.

**Tradeoffs.**
- HTTP constraints that used guidance now use xgrammar by default. Schemas with keywords xgrammar ignores (`multipleOf`, `uniqueItems`/`contains`, unsupported string `format`s, `pattern` with length bounds, ...) return 400 instead of being enforced by guidance; `--structured-outputs-config '{"backend": "guidance"}'` restores that. llguidance does not implement `uniqueItems` either: Python `auto` rejects it in guidance validation, while the Rust frontend on `main` returns an empty 200 when the matcher errors in EngineCore.
- Lark grammars now compile with xgrammar's Lark support (#58321); llguidance-only extensions need `backend=guidance`.
- Schemas composed into a parser grammar are not checked for xgrammar-unsupported keywords, as in Python.
- `vllm-rs serve` reads only the JSON form of `--structured-outputs-config`; the dotted form (`--structured-outputs-config.backend guidance`) goes to the Python engine only, like other dotted flags on that path. The `vllm serve` path reads both.

**Not a duplicate.**
- #61892 (merged) moved gRPC to xgrammar and named this change as its follow-up.
- #62431 (open) no longer touches `--structured-outputs-config`; the two PRs are independent.
- #49625 (merged) makes EngineCore reject a request whose backend differs from the one it already uses, with `RequestError(code="validation_error")`. On `main` the Rust frontend's mixed traffic now hits that rejection instead of `KeyError: 'triggers'` (still a 500 in Rust, which does not map that code yet); with this PR every Rust request names the same backend, so the rejection is not reached. #62246 (draft) would let EngineCore hold several backends. This PR changes only what the Rust frontend sends.
- #55153 (open) teaches guidance some `format`-shape structural tags; with it, more guidance requests would pass the new check, which can be relaxed then.

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Moves DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's InferenceX AgentX lanes into tuned **presets** (vllm-project/recipes [SCHEMA.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/SCHEMA.md) `presets`). Each preset carries the lane's concurrency points, builder choices and image. Readers previously had to adjust the command by hand from tables in the guide. Same pattern as #63534 (MiniMax-M3) and #63552 (Kimi-K3, merged).

Relies on two renderer fixes, both merged:

- vllm-project/recipes#1178 sizes the DEP router from the engine's `--data-parallel-size`, which the DEP2/DEP4 presets set.
- vllm-project/recipes#1179 makes `json_args` edit-only on toggle flags, so unticking Speculative decoding leaves no half-built `--speculative-config`.

## Claims

**Six presets**, all scoped to `[fp8, default]`. The lanes served the 0909 checkpoint, so the JSON API renders them on 0909. The builder applies them to 1017 too, since it has the same format and memory layout.

| Preset | GPU · strategy | Default | Points | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `b200_agentx_tp` | B200 · TP | yes | TP4 c1/4/8/16/32/128, TP2 c1 | InferenceX #3837 |
| `b200_agentx_dep` | B200 · DEP | yes | DEP2 c8–32, DEP2 + host KV c64/128, DEP4 c96/128 | InferenceX #3837 |
| `b300_agentx_tp` | B300 · TP | opt-in, **new** | TP4 c1/8/16, specialized decode | InferenceX #4332 |
| `b300_agentx_dep` | B300 · DEP | opt-in, **new** | DEP2 c8–64, host KV c128/192 (Simple offload, 50 GiB/rank) | InferenceX #4332 |
| `mi355x_agentx` | MI355X · TP | opt-in, **new** | TP2 c1/2/4/8/16/32/64 (c16/c32 capped), TP4 c1/2 | InferenceX #4409 |
| `gb300_agentx_pd` | GB300 · PD | yes | unchanged DEP4 + DEP16 1P1D | InferenceX #3941 |

Every preset except GB300 PD also does the following:
- pins the lane image;
- selects Rust, Speculative decoding and Text only, with Encoder parallel off;
- turns adaptive verification off, as the lanes ran.

The DEP presets size the engine with `--data-parallel-size 2` or `4`, on part of the node.

**Guide:**
- The B200 per-concurrency tables, the B300 aggregate table and the MI355X TP2 scheduling table become the presets' points.
- The MI355X benchmark-server command (InferenceX #3058, an older revision of the #4409 lane) is removed. The opt-in preset renders the current lane.
- The **Dynamo disaggregated serving on B300 and GB300** section is untouched (#62711 edits it).

**Default renderings that change (intentionally):** B200 TP and DEP, plus the two Mooncake renderings that wrap the TP preset, which change image only. Each appears under both the 0909 and 1017 IDs, so 8 files in all, and every one now shows the lane as it ran:

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `hw/b200.json` (TP2 c1) | lane image; Speculative decoding with `enable_adaptive_verification:false`; `--language-model-only` instead of `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` |
| `hw/b200/strategies/single_node_dep.json` (DEP2 c32) | the same, plus `--data-parallel-size 2` (was 8) |
| `hw/b200/strategies/kv_store_*_mooncake.json` | lane image only |

Every other DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash rendering is identical (176 of 184 files). B300, MI355X and GB300 open on Baseline or their unchanged default as before.

## Validation

- `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <this checkout>/recipes` passes against recipes main.
- **First commit** (lane blocks moved into presets): every DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash rendering is identical to main.
- **Lane check:** a script expands each lane's srt-slurm config at the InferenceX commit pinned in `source.revision` and compares its server arguments and env with the preset point's rendering (renderer with #1178 and #1179). It covers every point the master rows run: 33 points across B200, B300 and MI355X. All match, with three equivalent exceptions:
  - The lanes pass vLLM defaults explicitly (`--tensor-parallel-size 1` under DEP, `--prefill-schedule-interval 1`).
  - MI355X sets `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True` where the recipe has `1`.
  - `--served-model-name`, `--max-model-len 1048576` and `--disable-uvicorn-access-log` are left out (the last is telemetry).
- **Builder (local):**
  - B200 opens on AgentX TP, TP2 at concurrency 1; the TP4 points switch TP. The DEP points switch DP2/DP4 on the engine and the router tab, with the new "runs DP=2 on 2 of 8 GPUs" hint.
  - Unticking Speculative decoding drops the spec config, and a reload keeps the point.
  - B300 AgentX DEP2's host-KV points turn on Simple offload at 50 GiB per rank.
  - MI355X AgentX TP2 switches TP2/TP4 on the pinned image.

## Details

- **Default vs opt-in.** B200 TP/DEP and GB300 PD already rendered their lanes for every user, so they stay default. Their remaining default changes are the image and builder choices the lanes ran with.
  - **B300** was opt-in because its lanes need a dev image: the specialized decode from #61868 (merged 2026-10-21) and its DSpark draft path from #61869 (still open).
  - **MI355X** was opt-in because its lane pins an image digest. The guide described it as a recommendation for AgentX-like traffic.
- **Baselines.** B200 TP keeps the Engram CPU offload TP2 needs outside the preset, so Baseline matches GB200/GB300. B200 DEP's Baseline is the shared Blackwell DEP8.
- **B200 DEP default point.** It is DEP2 c32, the engine settings B200 DEP already rendered. It now runs on two GPUs, as the lane does, instead of spanning all eight.
- **Router flags.** The lanes' `--request-timeout-secs 14400` and `--disable-retries` stay in the DEP runbooks; the router companion's command is fixed per strategy.
- **Point labels.** Points are labelled by the bare concurrency, with what else they change in parentheses (`8 (DEP2)`, `64 (DEP2 + host KV)`), since the builder titles the row Concurrency; vllm-project/recipes#1186 makes that the convention. The last commits relabel MiniMax-M3 (#63534) and Kimi-K3 (#63552) the same way: M3 said "8 clients" (also in its descriptions and GB200 table), K3 said `C8`. For these agentic lanes concurrency counts concurrent sessions.
- **Not in this PR:**
  - The B300/GB300 Dynamo xPyD lanes (#4231, #4266): several engines per node and per PD role aren't builder features.
  - GB300's single-node AgentX lanes: they aren't in the recipe today.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Add --reasoning-effort-map to rewrite request reasoning efforts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds a `--reasoning-effort-map` frontend flag that rewrites the reasoning effort a client sends into one the served chat template supports, before it reaches the chat template or the Harmony preamble.

Addresses #52738. Related: #52739 (see "Not a duplicate" below).

## Claims

- `--reasoning-effort-map '{"minimal": "low", "medium": "low", "xhigh": "max"}'` rewrites the listed efforts; unlisted efforts pass through unchanged.
- Applies to the effort set through Chat Completions (`reasoning_effort`), Responses (`reasoning.effort`) and Anthropic Messages (`output_config.effort`), on both the chat-template and Harmony paths.
- `enable_thinking` follows the mapped effort, so mapping to `none` disables thinking and mapping `none` to another effort enables it.
- A `reasoning_effort` set directly in `chat_template_kwargs` is not rewritten.
- Keys are validated at startup against the known efforts, so a typo fails `vllm serve` instead of being silently ignored.
- With the flag unset (default) behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

Unit tests added to existing suites:

- `test_cli_args.py`: the flag parses, and unknown keys / non-string values / non-object JSON are rejected at startup.
- `test_reasoning_enable_thinking.py`: listed efforts are rewritten and unlisted ones are not (Chat Completions and Responses), `enable_thinking` follows the mapped effort in both directions, and `chat_template_kwargs` bypasses the map.
- `test_render_parity.py`: with `{"none": "low"}`, Harmony renders `none` to the same prompt tokens as `low` (and different from `high`) instead of rejecting it.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
    tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_cli_args.py \
    tests/entrypoints/openai/test_reasoning_enable_thinking.py \
    tests/entrypoints/openai/test_render_parity.py \
    tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \
    tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py \
    tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py -q
```

Result: `350 passed, 1 xfailed, 15 errors`. All 15 errors were server-fixture startups in `test_serving_chat.py` and `test_batched_chat_completions.py` failing because GPU 0 on the dev box was occupied (`Free memory on device cuda:0 (18.17/79.18 GiB) ... is less than desired GPU memory utilization`). Rerunning those two files with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4`: `198 passed, 4 skipped`.

Not done: no end-to-end run against a served model whose template rejects or falls back on an effort, and no model eval. The change only alters the `reasoning_effort` value handed to the template, and only when the flag is set.

## Details

**Motivation.** The API accepts `none`/`minimal`/`low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max`, but chat templates recognize different subsets. Some raise on values they do not know (#52738), and others silently fall back to another effort, e.g. maximum reasoning. Clients such as agent harnesses often send a fixed effort that cannot be changed client-side, so operators need a server-side way to translate.

**Design.**

- The map is an explicit per-effort rewrite rather than an inferred one: the operator states exactly what each unsupported effort becomes. Values are passed to the template as-is and are not restricted to the API's effort names, since templates may define their own.
- It is applied where the effort is read off the request (`build_chat_params` for Chat Completions and Responses, and the two Harmony preamble builders) through one helper, `map_reasoning_effort`. The map lives on `OnlineRenderer`/`OnlineDerenderer`, so the API server and the render server behave the same. Anthropic Messages requests are converted to a `ChatCompletionRequest` and go through the same path.
- The `ReasoningEffort` literal moves to `vllm/renderers/params.py` so the request model and the startup validation share one definition.

**Limitations.**

- An effort passed in `chat_template_kwargs` bypasses the map; that is the escape hatch for sending a value to the template verbatim.
- The map is static per server; it does not inspect the template to discover which efforts it supports.

**Not a duplicate.** #52739 targets the same issue with `--supported-reasoning-efforts` plus `--reasoning-effort-rounding {down,up}`, rounding along a fixed ladder. This PR differs in that the mapping is explicit rather than rounded, it can map to and from `none` (#52739 always passes `none` through), values may be template-specific strings, and it is applied in the renderer so the render server is covered. #55432 (`--reasoning-effort-budgets`) maps efforts to `thinking_token_budget`, which is a different output. No other open PR was found for `reasoning effort map` / `reasoning_effort chat template`.
